title: Compare text with Excel's collation and numbers with Excel's near-equality in calc_func
description:
## Outcome
calc_func's comparison operators order and equate text the way Excel does (case-insensitive, with Excel's collation for spaces, punctuation and non-ASCII letters), and compare numbers with Excel's equality rule for nearly equal values, all through calc_func::invoke.

## Context
Split out of cfunc-m1.2 (2026-10-19) as its prerequisite, not as a follow-up. cfunc-m1.2's Do names comparison, and its kernel (crates/calc-func/src/catalogue/comparison.rs) refuses, with NotImplemented, any text ordering that is not ASCII letters and digits, the equality of non-ASCII texts that differ, and numbers within a relative 1e-13. Excel's collation is not documented precisely enough to write from documentation alone. The truth comes from the owner's capture of cfunc-m1.2's oracle workbook, whose comparison rows (="apple pie"<"banana", ="a"<"B", ="a-b"<"ab", ="é"="É", near-equal number pairs) measure it. Library: CalcFunc.

## Do
Implement the comparison rules the captured rows show, with a case comparing every comparison row through calc_verdict::judge against the capture.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m1.2 --platform windows --require-all
```
Every comparison row of cfunc-m1.2's oracle capture matches, and no comparison row is refused.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox.

## Out of scope
Locale-specific collation beyond the capture's locale (cfml-m2.6 owns locale services).
notes: From cfunc-m1.2 round 4 (2026-10-20, 5e0b3bb): comparison.rs numbers() now computes the near-equality band through Site::subtract and Site::multiply (it follows NumericMode). The band of a relative 1e-13 (NEAR) only marks which pairs are refused; Excel's rule comes from the owner's capture. Under Exact the refusal is wider (every pair of different numbers); routing that is cfunc-m3.22's.
close_reason: Closed in the bulk-port redirect (2026-10-23): built code on master with passing receipts; cargo xtask check passed on Windows for all 13 packages at 99edc1b (which includes cdoc-jpha 0e1dc39, dc-nzpw db130aa, dc-51ka 058ef2d, dc-xrxb 60f54b2). Remaining gaps belong to the work packages in docs/plan/BULK_PORT_PLAN.md.

comments.text:
Started 2026-10-21 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cdoc at f5a6059 (cfunc-m1.2's build commit, whose capture holds the 14 comparison rows this bead owns). It is cfunc-m1.2's prerequisite, and the Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b) needs it too: an exact MATCH, VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP with an ASCII key refuses the whole call when a non-ASCII text cell (a label such as one with a currency sign) comes before the match, and comparisons over such text refuse.
- The capability: calc_func's comparison (crates/calc-func/src/catalogue/comparison.rs, used by =, <>, <, <=, >, >= and by every lookup and criterion through comparison::texts) equates and orders text as Excel on this machine does, and compares nearly equal numbers by Excel's rule, through calc_func::invoke.
- Measure first: an oracle workbook from the committed generator with text pairs compared with = and < (ASCII letters, digits and punctuation, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes, letters with diacritics in Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A, ligatures, common symbols such as currency signs and the degree sign, and the 14 cfunc-m1.2 rows' kinds), and number pairs around the near-equality boundary (0.1+0.2 against 0.3, 1+1E-15 against 1, differences at the 15th, 16th and 17th significant digit, signs, zero and tiny values); capture it with `cargo xtask capture` and derive the rule from what Excel gives. Implement the measured rule for the repertoire the rows cover, and refuse text beyond it with a typed not-modelled refusal naming cfml-m2.6 (locale services).
- Cases: cdoc_jpha__text_and_number_comparison (rows through calc_func::invoke, each expected value labelled from the capture) and cdoc_jpha__excel_comparison (the workbook against its capture through calc_verdict), plus cfunc-m1.2's own accept: its comparison note must show no row left under cdoc-jpha.
- Keep calc_func's public API unchanged or extend it additively.
- What green does not show: collation in other locales (cfml-m2.6).

comments.text: 2026-10-21, from the Ofgem comparison re-run with cfunc-m3.6 on master (dc-3t1b): Annex-9's 252 MATCH roots are refused as a whole call (Function(NotImplemented { id: FunctionId(9.2), argument: None })) for an exact MATCH (match_type 0) whose key is built as cell&"_"&cell, over a lookup column of 84 ASCII text cells that each hold characters other than letters and digits (underscores, spaces, punctuation); no cell is non-ASCII. One VLOOKUP root in Default-tariff-cap-level refuses the same way (FunctionId(9.5)). So the equality calc_func's lookups use refuses ASCII text with punctuation, not only non-ASCII text: this bead's rule must cover exact equality of such text (as the lookups call it through comparison::texts), and a re-run of the Ofgem compare after it lands shows whether these 253 roots compute.

title: Define engine-neutral authored operations and revisions
description:
## Outcome
Define engine-neutral authored operations and revisions. The behaviour is available through the CalcDoc production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements §§2, 3, 7 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within Bootstrap checkpoint — independent lanes, CI and evidence safety. Own only CalcDoc files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: calc_doc::open / prepare_edit / prepare_save / write; inspect the emitted package independently.

## Do
In calc-doc-model define AuthoredRevision, immutable model roots, WorkbookOp batches, structural-edit descriptors, CellInput and document-only metadata. The operation schema contains no engine/session types and never serializes computed cache as authored input. Generate per-capability operation codecs.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
fresh; design these neutral types from this plan. OxDoc model names are not copied into the bootstrap contract.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p calc-doc --test acceptance cdoc_m0_1 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `cdoc_m0_1__op_roundtrip`: Every initially admitted operation round-trips through the versioned wire codec.
- `cdoc_m0_1__no_engine_dependency`: The model package compiles without CalcEngine, CalcFml or CalcHost and a cached value cannot be decoded as an authored formula replacement.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox. Run the same semantic fixtures on every target; platform adapters also have their native integration tests.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: cdoc-m0.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- Package and route. The types and the operation codec live in crates/calc-doc-model, which CalcEngine may depend on (never on calc-doc, the package codec). calc-doc-model depends on calc-value (plan 2.1, MODEL to VALUE). calc-doc depends on calc-doc-model and re-exports it, and the two named cases live in crates/calc-doc/tests/acceptance.rs, registered in crates/calc-doc/acceptance.json for windows, linux and wasm. The cases reach the types only through calc-doc's re-export. calc_doc::open, prepare_edit, prepare_save and write arrive with the cdoc-m1 beads; this bead adds none of them, and no stand-in.
- Port: fresh. OxDoc is not read for this bead, and none of its model names (nor its OxCalc* symbols) enter CalcDoc. No migration record.
- Initially admitted operations. WorkbookOp has exactly these variants:
  - SetCell { at: CellKey, input: CellInput }.
  - Clear { area: GridArea }, which clears authored contents.
  - EditAxis(AxisEdit): insert or delete rows or columns on one sheet, with 1-based checked positions, a count of at least 1, within the grid.
  - EditSheet(SheetEdit): insert, rename, move, remove, and set visibility.
  AxisEdit and SheetEdit are the structural-edit descriptors. The other families in plan 2.2's sketch (Fill, MoveCells, EditName, EditTable, EditRule, EditStyle, EditObject, EditSettings, EditSkinLayout) are added by the beads that implement them, and the report names, from docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md, the bead that owns each.
- CellInput:
  - Number: a finite binary64, keeping -0.0 and subnormals.
  - Text: ExcelText, keeping its code units, a dangling surrogate included.
  - Logical.
  - Error: WorksheetErrorCode.
  - Formula: the formula's source text and nothing else, so no cached value and no parse result.
  No variant holds a calculated value.
- Document-only metadata: facts the engine never reads, starting with sheet visibility (visible, hidden, very hidden), which a SheetEdit sets.
- AuthoredRevision is a u64 newtype with a checked next. OpBatch { base: AuthoredRevision, operations } holds WorkbookOps only. This deviates from plan 2.2's sketch on purpose: that sketch's OpBatch also carried a CommandSource and SessionOps. SessionOps are session types, which this Do excludes. The command source and undo grouping belong to CalcHost's journal (chost-m1 and chost-m2.2).
- Model root: an immutable, Arc-shared ModelRoot holding its AuthoredRevision and the sheets in order, each with its SheetId, SheetKey, name and visibility. It has no cell storage yet; the cdoc-m1 beads and ceng-m1.1 add authored pages.
- IDs on the wire. calc-value's IDs are allocator-scoped and have no raw constructor (cfunc-m0.1), and a retained journal must replay in a later session (chost-m2.2, chost-m6.4). So the wire never carries a SheetId. Each sheet has a document-stable SheetKey: a u32, unique and never reused within one document (the xlsx sheetId attribute plays that role). The model root maps SheetKey to SheetId; the wire carries SheetKeys, and decoding resolves them through the receiving model root. An unknown key is a typed decode error. A SheetEdit insert carries the new sheet's SheetKey; its SheetId is issued when the edit is applied, which is the cdoc-m1 beads' work.
- Wire codec:
  - One codec per capability (cells, axes, sheets), each generated from that capability's declaration.
  - An envelope names the capability and its version.
  - An unknown capability, a newer version, an unknown field or a non-finite number is a typed refusal, never a silent drop.
  - serde =1.0.229 (with derive) and serde_json =1.0.154 may be normal dependencies of calc-doc-model; both are already in Cargo.lock and license-reviewed through xtask.
  - Numbers travel as their binary64 bits in hex (plan 10.1: no decimal round trip). Text travels as UTF-16 code units, so a dangling surrogate survives.
- Case cdoc_m0_1__op_roundtrip covers every admitted variant, every CellInput kind, and every AxisEdit and SheetEdit kind:
  - Encoding and then decoding through a model root gives the original.
  - Committed golden fixture files decode to the expected operations and re-encode byte for byte. The fixtures live in crates/calc-doc/tests/fixtures/ and are read with include_bytes!, so the browsers read the same bytes.
  - The edge values are -0.0, the smallest subnormal, the largest finite, a 32,767-unit text, a text ending in a high surrogate, every WorksheetErrorCode, and XFD1048576.
  - A newer version or an unknown capability is refused.
- Case cdoc_m0_1__no_engine_dependency has three parts:
  - The case computes calc-doc-model's dependency closure from the committed Cargo.lock bytes, read through include_str! so the browsers run the same check, and finds none of calc-engine, calc-fml, calc-host or calc-doc. Cargo.lock lists every target's and feature's edges, so this over-approximates the real closure.
  - A wire batch whose formula input also carries a cached value is refused, and so is a message holding a calculated value.
  - A value literal never decodes as a formula.
- wasm: AGENTS.md's browser-test convention (wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and wasm-bindgen-test =0.3.67 as wasm32-only dev-dependencies) applies to calc-doc and to calc-doc-model if it has unit tests.
- seams.json of calc-doc-model and calc-doc: every pub enum variant and trait is listed, with a non-test caller that its named case executes. Entries whose callers are all inside calc-doc-model are counted, and the orchestrator files their follow-up, as dc-0oyu does for calc-value.
- Adversarial class (M0 exit bead): refuters and judge at xhigh effort, and a mutation probe after the build commit, before the push.
Rulings after rounds 1 and 2 (2026-10-15):
- The golden fixtures are checked on their own. The case reads them as plain JSON and compares every operation's members with literal values written in the test. A claim that they came from a separate writer is not kept, because the writer was not kept.
- Limits stated on the items they concern rather than checked here, each with its owner in the tracker:
  - a batch acting on a sheet it inserts earlier, or on one it removed earlier: cdoc-m4.3;
  - never reusing a removed sheet's key: cdoc-m4.3;
  - comparing the batch base with the root's revision: chost-m1.1;
  - wire integers above 2^53 for browser-side readers: chost-m1.1;
  - formula length: cdoc-m1.2;
  - Excel's sheet-name rules: dc-85qk.
- Follow-ups filed: dc-kzkj (calc-doc-model seams entries with callers outside calc-doc-model; blocks dc-pz3u), dc-7qtj (a calc-doc-model layering rule in architecture.json) and dc-85qk. The beads that own the other WorkbookOp families (cdoc-m4.2, cdoc-m3.1, cdoc-m3.2, cdoc-m5.2, cdoc-m5.3, cdoc-m3.6, cdoc-m6.1, cdoc-m3.5, cdoc-m6.3, cdoc-m6.5 and cdoc-m2.1) each carry a note.
- The production route calc_doc::open, prepare_edit, prepare_save and write is absent by the claim ruling; the cdoc-m1 beads add it. Under `cargo xtask ci wasm`, the lib targets of calc-doc-model and calc-doc record zero_tests, because the cases live only in the acceptance target.
Ruling after round 3 (2026-10-15/17): the round-3 judge closed the build loop with no blocking finding. The refuters' surviving mutants are test-strength defects found before the probe, so they are fixed in a further commit on this bead after the build commit, as AGENTS.md provides. They are: the frame reader defaulting a missing base, version, operations or format; a negative integer read as u64; lenient visibility, error-name or hex-unit spellings; an AxisEdit::last off-by-one; ModelRoot accessors no case observes; and FiniteNumber's bitwise equality. The same commit states the formula-length and 2^53 limits on their items and corrects two doc comments and two Display messages. The mutation probe then runs on that fix commit.
close_reason:
Product status: calc-doc-model defines CalcDoc's engine-neutral authored contract, and calc-doc re-exports it as calc_doc::model:
- AuthoredRevision;
- an immutable, Arc-shared ModelRoot of sheets (SheetId, document-stable SheetKey, SheetName, SheetVisibility);
- OpBatch of WorkbookOps (SetCell, Clear, EditAxis, EditSheet);
- CellInput (finite number, text, logical, error, formula text; never a calculated value);
- one generated wire codec per capability (cells, axes, sheets), behind a versioned envelope and frame, with exact numbers and text and a typed refusal for every unknown or malformed input.
By the claim ruling, the production route calc_doc::open/prepare_edit/prepare_save/write is absent; the cdoc-m1 beads add it.
Evidence: build commit d8570dd and fix commit 8c7eae0.
- Windows: cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all exit 0, "ACCEPT passed cdoc_m0_1__op_roundtrip", "ACCEPT passed cdoc_m0_1__no_engine_dependency", "2 selected, 2 passed ... architecture checks 7/7 passed".
- wasm: --platform wasm --require-all exit 0, both cases "ran in Chrome" and "ran in Firefox".
- Linux, in the WSL clone at 8c7eae0: --platform linux --require-all exit 0, "2 selected, 2 passed".
- Receipts: accept-receipts/cdoc-m0.1/{windows,wasm,linux}.json.
- The fix commit makes the cases fail on 16 mutants the refuters had left green (fix/probes-final).
- Mutation probe on 8c7eae0: 10 of 10 breaks caught.
  - A shared byte-order swap, shared text truncation and a shared corner swap failed at the golden fixtures.
  - An unknown-key fallback, admitted newer versions, a cached value beside a formula, an axis edit past the grid's end, an undispatched capability and a wrong revision accessor each failed at their rows.
  - Without the browser attribute, no_engine_dependency was missing in both browsers.
- Regressions at 8c7eae0, all exit 0: Windows accepts of infra-m0.1 (with independent_lanes), m0.2, m0.3, m0.4, m0.5, dc-e8ql and cfunc-m0.1; cfunc-m0.1's wasm accept; cargo xtask ci wasm; cargo xtask ci licenses.
Still open:
- The 50 seams entries of calc-doc-model are counted as reach unproven (dc-kzkj, before dc-pz3u).
- dc-7qtj (layering rule) and dc-85qk (Excel's sheet-name rules).
- Limits stated on their items, with owners noted on cdoc-m4.3, chost-m1.1 and cdoc-m1.2: batch-internal sheet references, key reuse, the base revision, formula length, and integers above 2^53.
- Under cargo xtask ci wasm, the lib targets of calc-doc-model and calc-doc report zero_tests, because the cases live only in the acceptance target.
- CI push run 39104574184 was in progress when this bead closed.

title: Implement bounded ZIP package reading and raw preservation
description:
## Outcome

## Context
Implements §§2, 3, 7 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within First functional milestone — real Excel open/recalc/edit/save/reopen. Own only CalcDoc files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: calc_doc::open / prepare_edit / prepare_save / write; inspect the emitted package independently.

## Do
Open an .xlsx OPC package into a seekable backing source, a part directory and lazy XML readers. Reject zip-slip, external entity expansion and declared-size bombs under explicit resource limits. Retain untouched compressed payloads and relationship/content-type information.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

OxDoc/crates/oxdoc-model/src/lib.rs (5,939 lines in one file: serde model types; 191 engine-named OxCalc* symbols such as OxCalcCell, OxCalcCellInput, OxCalcCellValue and OXCALC_INGEST_INTERFACE_V1 that must not enter CalcDoc); OxDoc/crates/oxdoc-xlsx/src/lib.rs (37,648 lines in one file: OPC package reader/writer, source preservation and fidelity ledger, the RoundTripRefusal typed-refusal taxonomy near line 1204, WriteMode::FreshExport Save As, and the W010 tranche-2 authoring landed 2026-09-15: cell add, formula add/remove/change, sheet lifecycle); OxDoc/crates/oxdoc-conformance/ (10,934 lines of fixture-driven round-trip checks); OxDoc/docs/SPEC.md, DOCUMENT_LIFECYCLE_AND_HOST_BOUNDARIES.md and STRICT_LAZY_PARSING_SCOPE.md. The source exists locally (verified 2026-10-12) but has not been audited line by line: resolve the exact symbols in the infra-m0.4 manifest before copying, port behaviour (preservation, refusals, lazy profiles, authoring) rather than the monolithic file layout, and keep every OxCalc-named type out of the new crates.

## Acceptance
```text

cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m1.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m1.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `cdoc_m1_1__raw_preservation`: An independently read hash of every untouched part payload is unchanged after a no-op save.
- `cdoc_m1_1__malformed_zip`: Path traversal and adversarial expansion fail with typed errors and no filesystem writes.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox. Run the same semantic fixtures on every target; platform adapters also have their native integration tests.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: cdoc-m1.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.
Noted by infra-m0.4 (2026-10-14): OxDoc has no license file, so all 189 pinned OxDoc inputs read license none-found. Before copying any of them, confirm the owner's license decision for OxDoc; if it is still open, follow the unclear-license rule (file an Infrastructure disposition bead and make it a blocker of this bead).

Claimed 2026-10-19 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cdoc.
- Written fresh. OxDoc has no license file, so nothing is copied from it; its docs and code may be read for behaviour only.
- The capability to show: calc_doc::open reads an .xlsx package (one built by a committed generator, as platform/calc-oracle-excel/tests/fixtures/make-fixtures.ps1 builds them) into a part directory with lazy XML readers. Every untouched part's compressed payload, relationships and content types survive a no-op save, checked by hashing the written zip's entries independently. Zip-slip, external entities and declared-size bombs fail with typed errors under explicit limits, with no filesystem writes.
- A new dependency, such as a zip crate, needs its license entry in tools/xtask/licenses.json, and `cargo xtask ci licenses` must pass.
- What green does not show: that Excel opens the saved package (infra-m1.3), or cell and formula loading (cdoc-m1.2).
close_reason:
Product status: calc_doc::open reads .xlsx packages into a part directory with content types, relationships and lazy XML readers, under explicit limits with typed refusals (zip-slip, DOCTYPE and entities, declared-size bombs, CRC and length mismatches). A no-op save preserves every untouched entry byte for byte. Deflate is miniz_oxide and XML is quick-xml, both license-reviewed.
Evidence:
- Commit 1d290e9.
- accept windows passed (2 of 2) and wasm passed in Chrome and Firefox (lane clone DnaCalc-cdoc).
- accept linux in WSL at 1d290e9 passed (2 of 2), with dc-73yy 1 of 1. The infra-m0.3 regression passed on the combined tree.
- A refuter's mutations of the decoder bound each turned the malformed_zip case red.
Still open: cdoc-qhau owns the compressed-payload bound and trailing DEFLATE bytes; ZIP64 has no owner yet.

notes:
Provisional plan ID: cdoc-m1.2. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

From cdoc-m0.1 (2026-10-15): calc-doc-model's FormulaText refuses only empty text, so a formula of any length decodes. Loading must apply Excel's formula-length limit, or CalcFml's parser must, with a witness. calc-doc-model's SheetName rules (31 UTF-16 units, the forbidden characters, apostrophes) also apply to loaded names; their Excel measurement is owned by dc-85qk.

Claimed 2026-10-19 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cdoc after cdoc-m1.1 lands.
- Written fresh. OxDoc has no license file, so nothing is copied from it; it may be read for behaviour only.
- The capability to show: calc_doc::open loads workbook.xml's sheets and their relationships and each sheet's cells into a calc-doc-model ModelRoot, using dc-73yy's pages and a constructor that builds a filled root at the document's first revision.

title: Bound compressed-payload reads, refuse trailing DEFLATE bytes, and report dropped gap bytes in calc-doc
description:
## Outcome
calc-doc bounds every read of an untrusted package by what the entry declares: a compressed payload larger than its declared size allows is refused before it is read into memory, bytes after the final DEFLATE block are refused, and a no-op save reports the gap bytes it drops.

## Context
Found by cdoc-m1.1's round-2 judge (2026-10-19). crates/calc-doc/src/zip/mod.rs read_content reads entry.compressed_size bytes, checked only against the central directory offset, so an entry declaring a few KiB can allocate up to max_package_bytes (1 GiB) on read_part or at open; decompress_to_vec_with_limit returns on Done without checking that the whole input was consumed; SaveReceipt does not report dropped gap bytes (plan 7.2 asks for fidelity risk to be reported). Library: CalcDoc.

## Do
Refuse an entry whose compressed size exceeds the bound its declared size allows, before reading it; refuse trailing bytes after the final block; report dropped gap bytes in SaveReceipt.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
cdoc_m1_1__malformed_zip gains an entry with an oversized compressed payload (refused with a typed error, allocation bounded) and one with bytes after the final block (refused); cdoc_m1_1__raw_preservation asserts the receipt's dropped-byte count (37 on its fixture).

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox.

## Out of scope
ZIP64 support.
notes:
Claimed 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cdoc. Opening an untrusted workbook must never allocate far beyond what its entries declare or accept trailing data; this closes the gaps cdoc-m1.1's judge found.
- An entry's compressed payload larger than its declared uncompressed size allows (DEFLATE's worst-case expansion bound for that size, or stored size equal to declared size) is refused with a typed error before any of it is read into memory; a case shows the allocation stays bounded (an instrumented or counted read, not a timing).
- Bytes after the final DEFLATE block of an entry are refused with a typed error.
- SaveReceipt reports the gap bytes a save drops (37 on cdoc_m1_1__raw_preservation's fixture), and the case asserts the count.
- The cases are cdoc-m1.1's (malformed_zip and raw_preservation), as the bead's Acceptance says; cdoc-m1.2 and cdoc-m1.3 must keep passing (they read packages through the same code).
close_reason: Built at 83e5845: calc-doc refuses a deflated payload past the bound its declared size allows (block expansion plus 1 KiB for flush markers) before the part read reads any of it, refuses bytes after the final DEFLATE block, grows its decoder buffer with each allocation no larger than the declared size, and SaveReceipt reports dropped gap bytes (37 on cdoc_m1_1__raw_preservation's fixture). cdoc-m1.1, cdoc-m1.2 and cdoc-m1.3 pass 2 of 2 each on windows, wasm (Chrome and Firefox) and Linux (WSL, at 83e5845). title: Generate the initial function catalogue and call interface
description:
## Outcome
Generate the initial function catalogue and call interface. The behaviour is available through the CalcFunc production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements §§2, 5, 10 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within First functional milestone — real Excel open/recalc/edit/save/reopen. Own only CalcFunc files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: calc_func::invoke through the generated catalogue; do not call a detached test implementation.

## Do
Create a single logical declarative catalogue from per-family source fragments with explicit stable IDs; generate IDs, metadata, dispatch, signature help and oracle selection. Different family-port agents own different fragments, not one shared registry source file. Add FunctionCallTarget::invoke with caller-owned EvalServices and scratch. Admit arithmetic, comparison, concatenation, SUM and IF metadata for the thin slice; expose lazy argument policy rather than eager-evaluating IF.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
OxFunc/crates/oxfunc_core/src/function.rs: FunctionMeta; crates/oxfunc_core/src/function_call.rs: FunctionCallTarget, FunctionCallScratch, FunctionExecutionContextBundle; crates/oxfunc_core/src/registry.rs; crates/oxfunc_core/src/functions/surface_dispatch.rs. Paths after the first are relative to OxFunc/.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p calc-func --test acceptance cfunc_m1_1 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m1.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m1.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `cfunc_m1_1__catalogue_consistency`: Dispatch, help and arity data enumerate exactly the same admitted IDs.
- `cfunc_m1_1__unknown_function`: Unknown IDs return a typed registration error without dispatch by a second string switch.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox. Run the same semantic fixtures on every target; platform adapters also have their native integration tests.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: cfunc-m1.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

From cfunc-m0.1 (2026-10-15): calc-value does not port OxFunc's ValueBoundary. This bead's call interface carries two of its dropped witnesses: raw_function_return_allows_empty_but_not_missing_or_null (a raw function return may be Empty, never Missing or null) and reference_boundary_only_allows_reference_like (a reference-only parameter admits only references). migration/ports/cfunc-m0.1.json records them.

Claimed 2026-10-19 by the DnaCalc session (lane clones not running; capability first).
- Port: OxFunc function.rs and registry.rs (lookup exit 0). function_call.rs (exit 6) may be ported only against a fresh dispatch, because it calls surface_dispatch.rs. surface_dispatch.rs (exit 5) is not read at all; the dispatch is generated fresh from the catalogue.
- The capability this bead must show, beyond its two named cases: calc_func::invoke reaches SUM through the generated catalogue and returns 6 for the numbers 1, 2 and 3, and IF's metadata declares lazy arguments that the call interface does not evaluate early. Coercion of text and booleans belongs to cfunc-m1.2.
- What green does not show: that any function other than SUM computes, or that the catalogue covers more than the thin slice.
- Review: one implementer, refuters and judge at normal effort, and the orchestrator re-runs the acceptance.
close_reason:
Product status: calc-func has its generated catalogue (17 entries with stable IDs, from five family fragments) and calc_func::invoke. SUM(1,2,3) computes to 6 through the catalogue, IF is declared lazy and invoke asks for none of its arguments, and unknown IDs and names are refused with typed errors. Only SUM computes; cfunc-m1.2 owns coercion, arithmetic, comparison and IF's kernel.

title: Commit authored and engine edits as one transaction
description:
## Outcome
Commit authored and engine edits as one transaction. The behaviour is available through the CalcHost production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements §§2, 3, 8 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within First functional milestone — real Excel open/recalc/edit/save/reopen. Own only CalcHost files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: calc_host::dispatch / step / project / save through a real HostState, not a parallel session.

## Do
Create HostState owning the document and EngineState. Translate a command to one WorkbookOp batch; prepare document and engine effects, preflight reservations, then commit both without fallible allocation. Roll back preparation on error; publish one authored revision and a dirty set.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
DnaTreeCalc/src/dnacalc-host-core/src/workbook.rs: WorkbookSession, XlsxSourceState; DnaTreeCalc/src/dnacalc-host-core/src/command.rs: HostCommand; src/dnacalc-host-core/src/grid_publication.rs (relative to DnaTreeCalc). Use these as behavioural references only; replace engine-owned authoring.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p calc-host --test acceptance chost_m1_1 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id chost-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id chost-m1.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id chost-m1.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `chost_m1_1__atomic_prepare_failure`: Failure after document preparation leaves both original revisions and all cell contents unchanged.
- `chost_m1_1__recalc_failure_keeps_edit`: A committed edit survives a later recalc failure while old computed values become Stale.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox. Run the same semantic fixtures on every target; platform adapters also have their native integration tests.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: chost-m1.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

From cdoc-m0.1 (2026-10-15): calc-doc-model's decode_batch does not compare a batch's base AuthoredRevision with the receiving root's revision. That check belongs to the host's commit, which rejects a batch prepared against another revision. Integers in the wire frame (the base included) travel as JSON decimal u64, so a browser-side reader that parses them as JavaScript numbers would lose precision above 2^53; the host's worker messages must not round-trip them through JSON.parse numbers.

From ceng-m1.2's review (2026-10-20). (1) The engine trusts its single caller: finish accepts a RecalcWork from another EngineState, a same-revision foreign snapshot is accepted, and set_prerequisites can replace a bound node's edges (dc-odsu hardens these); CalcHost, as the one mutation owner, must never do any of them. (2) Wire calc-doc's loaded FileCached caches into EngineState::with_file_caches, and show in a host case that caches loaded from package bytes are never scored as Calculated (the engine case builds them in memory). (3) EngineState::result()/results() still return the old Calculated result for cells stale() lists: label those Stale at the host (plan 2.2 ValueProvenance::Stale). (4) The engine's data flow differs from plan 2.2's sketch: begin_recalc takes &mut EngineState and finish installs the generation instead of returning a PreparedPublication; RecalcRequest, CalcContext and EffectTape are absent. Fit the paired commit around a mutating finish, or record the deviation.

Started 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the main clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc (br refuses the claim while ceng-m1.2 is open; its build is on master at a4f4d5d and waits only on its Linux run). This is the first bead where a document edit and the engine's recalculation are one transaction.
- Port: the DnaTreeCalc files are behaviour references only; look each up with `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` and record the exits in migration/ports/chost-m1.1.json; nothing is copied unless a lookup exits 0. Written fresh otherwise.
- The capability to show, through calc_host::dispatch / step / project over a real HostState:
  - HostState owns the opened and loaded document (calc_doc::open + calc_doc::load, the current calc-doc-model ModelRoot revision) and the calc_engine::EngineState built from that snapshot, with calc-doc's loaded FileCached caches passed to EngineState::with_file_caches. It is the only mutation owner of both.
  - dispatch translates a command (set a value, set a formula, clear a cell or area on an existing sheet) into one WorkbookOp batch whose base is the current authored revision (a batch prepared against another revision is refused: the cdoc-m0.1 note). It prepares the document side (calc_doc::prepare_edit) and the engine side (calc_engine::prepare_edit, reserving node IDs and seeds) against the same base, and only then commits both, with no fallible allocation after the first commit step. Any failure before that drops both preparations: the authored revision, the engine generation and every cell are unchanged.
  - A committed edit publishes one new authored revision and the dirty set (the engine's seeds and pending nodes).
  - step drives begin_recalc / step / finish to a published generation. A recalculation failure keeps the committed edit (the authored revision stays advanced) and the host labels every published result the engine lists in stale() as Stale (plan 2.2 ValueProvenance::Stale), never as Calculated.
  - project returns each requested cell's input and value with its provenance: authored literal, FileCached (from the package, never scored as Calculated), Calculated{revision, tick, mode}, Stale, or not modelled.
- Never call EngineState::set_prerequisites, never mix RecalcWork or snapshots across states (the ceng-m1.2 review; dc-odsu hardens the engine side).
- Cases:
  - chost_m1_1__atomic_prepare_failure: a failure injected after the document side is prepared (a typed refusal from the engine side or a reservation failure) leaves both revisions, the engine generation and every cell's input and value unchanged, observed through project.
  - chost_m1_1__recalc_failure_keeps_edit: an edit is committed, the recalculation fails (an injected observer stop or a read failure), the edit is present at the new authored revision, and the dependent cells' old Calculated values are projected as Stale.
  - Also: a workbook loaded from package bytes (a generator-built .xlsx with deliberately wrong formula caches) projects its caches as FileCached, never Calculated, until the host's first recalculation computes them.
- Out of this bead: save and delta projections (chost-m1.2); the observation hook for the verdict (dc-qguw).
- What green does not show: agreement with Excel (infra-m1.3's round trip).

Round 2 (2026-10-20): the judge did not close it on one item, the conservative StaleCause::FileCacheUnverified with no owning bead; the orchestrator fixes it inline (dc-f92f owns the replacement, the doc and ACCEPT-NOTE state what the cause counts). Ruling: dc-f92f is a follow-up, not a prerequisite. Neither named case requires an unreached cache to stay FileCached after an edit; the claim note's 'Also' holds in its no-edit reading (caches are FileCached before any input edit and after a no-change commit); the failure 'a dependent cell stays file-cached after an edit' cannot occur, because the host is stricter. Deviation from plan 2.2: calc_host::step takes a `&mut dyn ReadObserver` beside the budget, the hook dc-qguw extends for the evaluation record.

title: D4b: DNA Calc grid for everyday work: number formats, sizes, ranges, copy/paste, fill, insert/delete
description:
## Outcome
DNA Calc's grid skin behaves like Excel's for everyday work: cells show their number formats, columns and rows keep the workbook's sizes, and a user can select ranges, rows and columns, copy, paste, fill and insert or delete rows and columns, with undo.

## Context
D4 (dc-rif) built the shell, the grid, notebook and atlas skins on calc_host. Still missing there: number formats (General only), column widths and row heights, range/row/column selection, copy/paste, fill, structural edits (calc-host commands come from D2, dc-35p), tree and canvas skins, calc-doc's saved layout for notebook/tree/canvas, defined names in the atlas, a native desktop shell. The DTC workbook takes 13 s to open in the browser against 1.75 s natively.

## Do
- Number formats: render values through Excel's format codes (calc-func's TEXT formatter is the one formatter; extend it, never copy), read from calc-doc's styles via calc_host.
- Column widths and row heights from the workbook; hidden rows and columns.
- Range, row and column selection; copy and paste (values and formulas with relative references moved, through calc_host intents); fill down and right.
- Insert and delete rows and columns through calc_host's structural-edit commands, with undo.
- Measure the browser open time of the DTC workbook and file what makes it slower than native.

## Acceptance
Each item works in the browser smoke test (cargo xtask app smoke calc) in Chrome and Firefox; cargo xtask check --wasm passes; a saved workbook reopens in Excel without repair.

description:
## Outcome

title: Parallel evaluation for a full recalculation on native platforms
description:
## Outcome
A full recalculation evaluates independent formulas on several threads on native platforms, with results identical to the one-thread order, so DTC's full recalculation approaches Excel's.

## Context
dc-10d9 (bdf33b3): DTC full recalculation DNA 1.305 s on one thread vs Excel CalculateFull 0.061 s on 16 threads. Per-formula cost on one thread is close to Excel's per-thread cost (2.2-3.0 Gcycles for 165,810 formulas), so the gap is mainly threads. The evaluator, graph and verdict path stay one of each (AGENTS.md honesty rule 4); wasm keeps the one-thread path unless web workers are added.

## Do
Design and implement parallel evaluation over the dependency order (levels or a work-stealing ready queue), keeping volatile, dynamic-dependency (INDIRECT, OFFSET) and spill behaviour exact; test that every Ofgem cell and the oracle corpus give the same result with 1 and N threads.

## Acceptance
cargo xtask bench before/after on all three Ofgem workbooks; Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272 at 1 and N threads; cargo xtask check --wasm passes.
close_reason: A full recalculation evaluates independent formulas on several threads on native platforms through the one evaluator (evaluate_with reads shared read-only state and writes only thread-local storage; every write to the recalculation is made on the calling thread in order; a formula that reads something not yet calculated is re-evaluated serially in its place; random streams are keyed by seed, tick and cell, so they do not depend on order). Results equal the one-thread run: cargo xtask bench --verify-threads compared every Ofgem formula cell after 7 recalculations per workbook at 4, 8 and 16 threads, 0 differences; Ofgem 209,272/209,272; oracle workbooks equal at 1/4/8/16 threads (calc-host tests/threads.rs); D2 differential sessions pass on 4 threads; cargo xtask check and check --wasm pass. DTC full recalculation 0.655 s -> 0.311 s median (0.247 lowest) at 8 threads, Excel CalculateFull 0.049 s on 16; DTC one-cell edit (83,547 formulas) 0.487 -> 0.227 s, Excel 0.226 s; Annex 4 full 0.097 -> 0.036 s (Excel 0.009); Annex 9 0.081 -> 0.042 s at 16 (Excel 0.014). Machine shared with three cargo jobs, so medians are noisy. Commits 05e1ab2, 3b0e25b, f15aafa. Still open (dc-dxm): staging and finishing on one thread; arrays, spills, cycles and data tables stay on one thread; 16 threads no faster than 8 on this 8-core machine; per-thread cost 3-4x Excel.

title: Evaluate formulas of Excel's maximum length without exhausting the stack
description:
## Outcome
A formula of Excel's maximum length (8,192 characters) parses, binds, compiles and evaluates through calc_fml without exhausting the stack, on a 1 MB thread in a debug build and in the browsers, or is refused with a typed error at a stated depth; the process never aborts.

## Context
Found by cfml-m1.3's round-2 review (2026-10-20). Lowering::expression (crates/calc-fml/src/eval/compile.rs, the BinaryExpr arm) recurses once per level of a left-deep chain: =1+1+...+1 with 180 terms (362 characters) overflows the 1 MB Windows main thread in a debug build and aborts the process. A release build survives 2,000 terms; the cfml-m1.2 binder overflows at 2,500 in release; wasm32's stack was not measured. Evaluation also recurses on the native stack (cfml-m2.3 owns the explicit stack). Such formulas are valid Excel. CalcFml files only.

## Do
- Make parsing, binding, lowering and evaluation of operator chains iterative, or bound their depth with a typed CompileError/EvalFault naming the depth, whichever keeps every formula Excel accepts working.
- State each recursion that remains, and its bound, in the code and the migration record.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p calc-fml --test acceptance cfml_m1_3 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id cfml-m1.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cfml-m1.3 --platform wasm --require-all
```
A case builds =1+1+...+1 of 8,192 characters and a 64-deep nest of IF, evaluates both on a thread with a 1 MB stack in the debug test build and in Chrome and Firefox, and asserts their values (4,096 and the innermost branch).

## Out of scope
The explicit evaluation stack for LET and LAMBDA (cfml-m2.3).
notes:
Started 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-ceng (br refuses the claim while cfml-m1.3 is open; its evaluator is on master).
- Register this bead's own case in crates/calc-fml/acceptance.json: dc_2mlz__maximum_length (windows, linux, wasm), with commands `cargo test -p calc-fml --test acceptance dc_2mlz` and the accept commands for dc-2mlz. The case builds =1+1+...+1 of exactly 8,192 characters (4,096 terms) and a 64-deep nest of IF, runs parse, bind, compile and evaluate through calc_fml's public API on a thread spawned with a 1 MB stack in the debug test build (natively) and on the browser's main thread in Chrome and Firefox, and asserts 4,096 and the innermost branch's value. Also a right-deep chain (=1+(1+(1+...))) at Excel's nesting limits and a deep parenthesised group, so no direction of nesting is left recursive without a bound.
- Prefer iterative lowering and evaluation of operator chains (an explicit work stack) over a depth bound; a bound is acceptable only where Excel itself bounds the depth (64 nested function calls), with a typed CompileError naming it. State every recursion that remains and its bound in the code and in migration/ports/cfml-m1.3.json (this bead amends cfml-m1.3's record; say so).
- Do not change calc_fml's public API (ceng-m1.2 and onecalc-m1.1 build on it in other clones now).

From cdoc-m1.3's review (2026-10-20): calc_doc::prepare_edit parses every authored formula, and dropping calc-fml's syntax tree for "1+".repeat(4095)+"1" (8,191 units) overflows the stack in Chrome debug wasm (RangeError in drop_in_place<calc_fml::syntax::tree::SyntaxNode>) and on the Windows debug main thread. The parser's tree drop is part of this bead: SyntaxNode's drop (and any recursive Clone/PartialEq/Debug the case reaches) must not recurse per level. When this lands, cdoc_m1_3__formula_authoring's boundary check goes back to the deep 8,191-unit chain (crates/calc-doc/tests/acceptance.rs).

Handover 2026-10-20: built and pushed (6be5816). Evidence complete: dc-2mlz windows, wasm (Chrome and Firefox) and linux --require-all 1 of 1; regressions cfml-m1.3, cfml-m1.2, cfml-m1.1 pass on windows and linux (and cfml-m1.3 on wasm); receipts committed. Judge closed it; the orchestrator's post-judge edits were wording only and the accepts were repeated. br refuses the close only because cfml-m1.3 is open (it waits on cfunc-m1.2's owner capture). Close with the reason drafted in the session when cfml-m1.3 closes; cite 6be5816.

title: Close cfml binding gaps found in cfml-m1.2 review
description:
## Outcome
calc_fml::bind_references gives a typed site, or a typed refusal, for every reference form the cfml-m1.2 review found unhandled, and the cfml_m1_2 cases fail under the mutants that survived that review.

## Context
Found by cfml-m1.2's round-3 review (2026-10-20). Each item is a binding defect in crates/calc-fml/src/reference/bind.rs or a case that does not exercise a rule. None of them stops cfml-m1.3: the evaluator binds through the same binder, so a fix here reaches it. CalcFml files only.

## Do
- `={A1}`: a reference inside an array constant is not a live operand (Binder::walk has no ArrayLiteralExpr arm, bind.rs:128-131). Give it a typed refusal; Excel refuses the entry.
- `=Sheet2!#REF!` is refused as QualifiedNonReference; give it the #REF! value route instead.
- `=#REF!(A1)` parses as an invoke and binds A1 on the anchor's sheet; refuse or bind it as Excel reads it. Restore that exact input to the acceptance case (it was changed to `=#REF!SUM(A1)`).
- `=$B`, `=$3`, `=$XFE`, `=Sheet2!$B`, `=Sheet2!$3` give no site and no diagnostic (bind.rs:156, 181-186); a `$` form cannot be a name, so each gets a typed refusal, and the unit test at bind.rs:444 changes with it.
- Two-sheet ranges: `=Sheet2!A1:Sheet1!B2` asks the catalogue four times; `=Nope!B3:Sheet2!D7` never binds or reports the Sheet2 end. Assert the request counts and the sites.
- Surviving mutants: `lone-outside-grid-always-refused` (bind.rs:181; assert `=A1+0`, `=IF(A1>0,1,2)` and `=A1*1048577` each give only the A1 site), `deleted-pair-not-one-sheet` and `external-span-left-not-one-sheet` (bind.rs:209; assert `=#REF!A1:#REF!B2` and `=[B.xlsx]S!A1:[B.xlsx]S!B2`). Each mutant must turn a cfml_m1_2 case red.
- read_cells with a multi-cell CellRun::Values run that wraps a row boundary (read.rs:139-153): a reader that returns such runs, and assertions on the cells and positions.
- Migration record cfml-m1.2.json: move AxisRef and ReferenceNotation to a written-fresh entry (coords.rs lookup exits 1), and drop the fields AGENTS.md does not list.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p calc-fml --test acceptance cfml_m1_2 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id cfml-m1.2 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cfml-m1.2 --platform wasm --require-all
```
Each mutant above, applied by hand, fails the first command; keep the diff and the failing output under target/accept/cfml-m1.2/.

## Out of scope
Excel measurement of these readings (the owner's capture bead). Name and LAMBDA binding (cfml-m3.1).
notes:
Claimed 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the main clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc while cfml-m1.3 is built in DnaCalc-cfml (it adds crates/calc-fml/src/eval/ and cfml_m1_3 cases; this bead stays in reference/ and the cfml_m1_2 cases, so the two merge).
- The capability: every reference form the cfml-m1.2 review found unhandled gets a typed site or a typed refusal, so cfml-m1.3's evaluator never receives a silently dropped or wrongly bound reference.
- Rulings: `={A1}` is a typed refusal (Excel refuses a reference inside an array constant at entry). `=Sheet2!#REF!` binds to a deleted-reference operand whose placement gives #REF!, as `#REF!A1` does. `=#REF!(A1)`: a typed refusal unless the parser reads it as Excel does; restore that exact input to the case. `$`-only forms (`=$B`, `=$3`, `=$XFE`, `=Sheet2!$B`, `=Sheet2!$3`) are typed refusals, never silent.

title: Resolve INDIRECT's A1 text to a reference through calc_fml, ahead of OFFSET and the reference operators
description:
## Outcome
INDIRECT(ref_text) with A1-style text (a cell, a range, a sheet-qualified range, quoted sheet names, absolute and relative forms) resolves through calc_fml's binder to the reference Excel resolves, so a formula such as INDEX(INDIRECT(sheet&"!$A$9:$BF$96"),...) computes through calc_fml::evaluate, and the evaluation reports the cells it read as a dynamic read footprint the engine can use; text Excel cannot resolve gives #REF!, as Excel does.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b, 2026-10-21): INDIRECT is the function-missing root of 252 cells in Default-tariff-cap-level, all of one shape, INDEX(INDIRECT(cell&"..."),MATCH(...,INDIRECT(...)),MATCH(...,INDIRECT(...))); calc_fml's compile refuses the name. INDIRECT sits in cfml-m3.3 with OFFSET and the reference operators (union, intersection, spill, @), whose scope is wider; this bead takes INDIRECT out of cfml-m3.3 so it lands now. Making the engine re-dirty and reschedule on the reads INDIRECT reports is ceng-m3.3's (dynamic read overlays), which follows. Library: CalcFml.

## Do
- INDIRECT as a catalogued call whose result is a reference resolved from text by calc_fml's binder in the formula's workbook context (sheet names, quoted names, $ forms, ranges, a whole column or row); a1=FALSE (R1C1 text) measured and implemented, or refused as not modelled naming cfml-m3.3; a defined name in the text refused as not modelled naming cfml-m3.3 unless the binder resolves names already.
- The evaluation reports the area INDIRECT resolved as a read footprint (the ReadObserver route), and INDIRECT is marked volatile if the catalogue has that property.
- Rows labelled documented or measured, an oracle workbook from the committed generator, `cargo xtask capture`, and a comparison case through calc_verdict, including INDIRECT nested in INDEX and MATCH as the Ofgem shape uses it, an unresolvable text (#REF!), and a reference to another sheet.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
Every row calc_fml computes matches the capture; rows another bead owns are published as not modelled under it.

## Out of scope
OFFSET and the reference operators (cfml-m3.3); the engine's dynamic dependency edges (ceng-m3.3).

title: Judge a capture whose shared-formula ref spans cells outside its group, as Excel saves them
description:
## Outcome
A CaptureRecord of an Excel-saved workbook is judged, not refused, when a shared-formula ref covers cells of other groups, normal formulas, constants or empty cells, so `cargo xtask capture` writes a record of real workbooks instead of exiting 5.

## Context
Measured 2026-10-21 on the three Ofgem price-cap workbooks downloaded with the owner's yes (C:\Work\DnaCalc\corpus\ofgem-price-cap-2026q4): 27 of 119 shared groups (Annex-4), 11 of 488 (Annex-9) and 103 of 2,581 (Default-tariff-cap-level) have refs whose cells include other shared groups, normal formulas, constants or styled empty cells; no group has a member outside its ref. calc-verdict's check_shared_ranges (tools/calc-verdict/src/verdict.rs) refuses any range cell that is not a group member, and `cargo xtask capture` runs that check through its file-cache replay, so no record of these files can be written. calc-doc already tolerates the holes (crates/calc-doc/src/load/sheet.rs).

## Do
- Keep: the range is on a listed sheet; one range per group; every group cell lies inside its range; every group has a range.
- Remove: every cell of the range must be a group cell. Say in the doc comment that completeness of the denominator rests on the worker's cross-check against Excel's own SpecialCells(xlCellTypeFormulas), whose failures already refuse the record.
- Update the unit test that pins the old message; note on infra-m1.3 that the rule was checked against real captures and changed here.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
A record whose shared ref C1:C8 lists 6 group cells, with a normal formula at C4 and no formula at C7, is judged with all 7 formula cells in the denominator; a group member outside its ref is still refused.

## Out of scope
Capturing the Ofgem workbooks (the Ofgem comparison bead).

title: Match Excel's bits on the six cells where the Ofgem comparison found a 1-ulp arithmetic difference
description:
## Outcome
calc_func's arithmetic gives Excel's binary64 result on the three formula shapes where the Ofgem comparison found DNA Calc 1 ulp away from Excel, or each is recorded as a measured bit variant with the operation that differs named.

## Context
The first `cargo xtask compare` of Ofgem Annex-4 and Annex-9 against this machine's Excel (dc-3t1b, 2026-10-21) found 3 kernel-bits cells out of 40,450 calculated; every other calculated cell matched. Each agrees with Excel to 15 significant digits and differs by 1 ulp, and in each the reads equal Excel's values (constants, or formula cells that matched):
- two Annex-4 cells of the shape IF(x="-","-",SUM(seven cells)*k+y) (DNA gives the correctly rounded IEEE result of a left-to-right SUM; Excel is 1 ulp away, one up and one down);
- one Annex-9 cell of the shape IFERROR(IF(a>0,a*(c/(b+c)),"0"),"-") (DNA gives the correctly rounded result of a*(c/(b+c)), which is also the exactly rounded value of the whole expression; Excel gives 1 ulp more).
Tested offline and ruled out: IEEE double with left-to-right evaluation, x87 80-bit intermediates for the sum and the product, division as multiplication by a reciprocal, and a*c/(b+c). The triage key (IF, IFERROR) is inferred; the difference lies in the arithmetic. The cell values are in the local compare output (C:\Work\DnaCalc\corpus\compare, outside the repository, licence unverified): commit no Ofgem values or text.
A function bit variant: recorded apart, it holds up no document, formula, engine or host work.

## Do
- In Excel on this machine, split each shape into its sub-expressions in separate cells (with the local Ofgem values, read-only, nothing committed) and find which operation's bits differ from IEEE double.
- Build synthetic reproducers of the same shape (searched values, not Ofgem's) as oracle rows from the committed generator, capture them, and find the rule (for example a summation order or precision in SUM, or an operation Excel does not round to nearest).
- Implement the rule if it is general and measured; otherwise record the rows as measured bit variants under this bead with a typed result kept and the difference counted.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
```
The synthetic rows match Excel's capture bit for bit, or each is published with its measured difference under this bead; a re-run of the Ofgem compare shows the three cells matched or still counted here.

## Out of scope
Other functions' bit differences (each its own bead).
close_reason: All 11 Ofgem cells that differed are fixed (db6dbf7): Excel does + - * / (and SUM, PRODUCT, AVERAGE, SUMSQ) in the x87 unit at 64-bit precision and then stores to binary64, so near-ties double-round to the other neighbour; the engine now does the same on x86_64, and off x86 (wasm) a portable emulation matches the hardware on 400,000 random pairs per operation. Evidence: Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272 (was 209,261); oracle rows for this rule 108 failing before, 0 after; cargo xtask check passed at a55c79c. Still open: other kernel bits under dc-j9k; the x87 function route in the browser under dc-8dg.

Each of the 11 Ofgem cells had an exact product, quotient or sum within 1/4096 ulp of a midpoint (e.g. Annex-4 products 0.4999 ulp from their rounding), so the double rounding goes to the even neighbour. calc-func Site arithmetic now uses excel_numeric::excel_x87_add/sub/mul/div; off x86_64 a portable emulation (excel_numeric::pc64) tested equal to the hardware. title: Scope goal: distributed, billion-node, typed and debuggable computation on Excel formulas
description:
## Outcome
DNA Calc stays based on Excel formulas, Excel functions and Excel's extensibility (LAMBDA, UDFs, add-ins). On that base it also offers what the owner's reference platform offers (Jane Street's Webs, a distributed, spreadsheet-like computation platform):
1. Distributed computation of one calculation domain across machines.
2. Incremental recomputation that scales to billions of nodes and edges, with recalculation work proportional to what changed.
3. Strong typing and rich data structures beyond traditional spreadsheet values, while the formula language stays Excel's.
4. Computations defined and edited both from Rust and from a web interface, through the same host route.
5. A formula debugger in the web interface that shows how a formula evaluated, on the one evaluator.
6. Performance at that scale, recorded with named scale workloads.

## Context
Recorded at the owner's request (2026-10-17) as a further scope goal. It is not part of the first version as plan section 11.2 and the plan header define it, and recording it changes no plan decision. The owner decides its placement (Owner questions below). The read-only mapping workflow wf_a31948f5-14a (2026-10-17) compared the goal with the plan, the tracker and the code; its findings follow.

Groundwork that exists:
- Engine state is supplied by the caller, and recalculation runs in budgeted steps (plan 2.2). Values, plans and input snapshots are immutable, Arc-shared and Send + Sync, and later frame-level parallelism against one snapshot is described (plan 3.5; cfunc_m0_1__send_sync).
- An evaluation step can request a dependency that is not ready, or yield (plan 2.2, 6.2). Async completions, pending-result tokens and external updates are versioned session operations (plan 8.8; cfml-m4.3, ceng-m4.6, chost-m4.11). Function metadata declares volatility, thread safety and async (cfunc-m4.1).
- Graph nodes exist only for formulas and participants, never for every coordinate. Ranges become interval edges, scheduling uses a ready queue with prerequisite counts and SCC condensation, an edit copies only bounded pages, and plans are shared across instances (plan 3.2, 4.1, 6.1, 6.2). Structural counters check all of this (infra-m7.8).
- Fast is deterministic across platforms, with identical effect tapes and bits (plan 5.4), so distributed results can be required to replay.
- The operation wire codec is versioned and exact, and names sheets by document-stable SheetKeys (cdoc-m0.1).
- Host dispatch is the one route for every caller, automation included (plan 2.2; chost-m4.12). Auditing must instrument the one evaluator (chost-m6.3), which is what a debugger needs.

Plan decisions the goal cuts across (owner decisions):
- One evaluator and one graph. Each workbook's mutation and calculation lane is serial, and no second parallel graph or evaluator is prebuilt in this phase (honesty rule 5; plan 3.5). Section 6 is the single-threaded reference strategy. Later strategies are admitted only behind the same operations and evaluator, checked by the differential twin (plan 6.5; ceng-m7.1). Distribution therefore has to be one graph partitioned under one ordered commit authority per domain (plan 3.3). It cannot be federated engines that exchange values in rounds (plan 6.1; ceng-m3.9).
- Excel only, with one formula language and no second DSL (executive decision; plan 4.2). Types must therefore be Excel's own (richData, entity and linked data types) or have an Excel-visible projection. A Rust definition API must produce Excel formulas, defined names and registered functions, because a computation lives in a cell or a defined name (plan header; 8.2).
- Persistence is xlsx with no sidecar, inside Excel's fixed grid (plan 8.2; calc-value grid bounds), so billions of nodes means many sheets, names or workbooks.
- No performance targets: measurements are recorded without thresholds, and a number is never called fast (plan header, 5.4, 10.4, 10.5; work prompt honesty inventory).
- Fast forbids uncontrolled reassociation (plan 5.4), so parallel or distributed reductions must keep a fixed order to stay replayable. Exact is native x86-64 only (plan 5.2).
- Portable packages cannot import networking (plan 1.3; os-imports check), so transport belongs in a native-only package under platform/.
- The browser hosts its own engine in a wasm32 worker (plan 3.5; dnacalc-m2.1). A web interface onto a shared or remote computation is a new host mode the plan does not describe.

Foreclosure risks in code that exists or comes next, cheapest to decide now:
- calc-value IDs (cfunc-m0.1, closed) are a u32 slot plus a u32 generation, which caps one workbook at about 4.29 billion node slots; the plan's sketch had u64. Slots live in a dense Vec, and calc-value declares no cargo features, so widening later breaks every consumer (crates/calc-value/src/id.rs).
- IDs are unique per allocator only, and NodeId has no document-stable key. Callable identity is a process-local Arc (crates/calc-value/src/value.rs). Cross-machine node and LAMBDA identity need a design.
- CoreValue is an exhaustive enum with no extension slot, and the 21 function-family ports will match on it. ArrayShape is usize, which is 32 bits on wasm32.
- ceng-m1.1 (the next engine bead) decides whether input pages are reached by in-process borrows or through a page-handle interface a remote partition could serve.
- cfml-m1.3 (a bottleneck bead) decides the plan and frame layout. Without an observation hook and a source-span map, a step debugger later means changing the evaluator. chost-m6.3 relies on a CalcFml trace policy that no bead owns.
- cfunc-m3.23 and cfunc-m3.4 decide the reduction order of aggregates under Fast.
- dnacalc-m2.1 decides whether its transport is independent of where the host runs.
- RecalcFacts is whole per-generation vectors (plan 2.2). AuthoredRevision is one u64 counter with one base per batch, which means one writer. ModelRoot handles sheets linearly (cdoc-m0.1), which is harmless at Excel's sheet counts.

## Do
An epic holds no work. Once the owner places this goal, a planning bead derives its child beads (as infra-m3.20 to infra-m3.24 do) and attaches them at these points:
- ceng-m7.1's strategy layer;
- ceng-m3.9's calculation domain;
- the async route of cfml-m4.3 and ceng-m4.6;
- dnacalc-m2.1's transport and a native-only transport package under platform/;
- chost-m4.12's programmatic route;
- auditing in chost-m6.3 and dnacalc-m6.19;
- infra-m7.8's named workloads;
- typed values in cdoc-m3.4, infra-m3.23 and cfunc-m3.19.

## Owner questions
1. Placement: a phase after the first version (after infra-m8.2), or do parts of it enter earlier?
2. ID width: keep calc-value's u32 slots, or widen them to u64 before cdoc-m0.1 closes and before ceng-m1.1 builds on them?
3. Typed values: exactly Excel's own data types, so that Excel opens them, or a DNA extension? And does CoreValue gain an extension slot now?
4. Performance: keep recorded workloads without thresholds, or set targets for named scale workloads? Targets would lift a plan rule.
5. Determinism: must parallel and distributed results stay bit-identical to the serial reference? A yes fixes the reduction order.
6. Anchoring: may a Rust-defined computation exist without a cell or defined-name anchor? The plan header and section 8.2 say no today.
7. Persistence: must every computation still open in Excel, or is a second store admitted for billion-node graphs?
8. Debugger timing: does formula auditing (chost-m6.3, M6, P3) move earlier, and which bead owns the CalcFml trace policy?

## Out of scope
Any change to the first version's scope, to the plan text or to build_plan.py until the owner rules on the questions above.
notes:
Owner rulings (2026-10-18):
- Question 2, ID width, is answered with option 1. calc-value keeps its 32-bit slots, and no ID is widened. Excel-size workbooks sit two to three orders of magnitude below the cap of about 4.29 billion slots per kind per workbook, and memory runs out long before that. Compact 32-bit slots keep the engine's edge lists small. If this goal is ever placed, scale beyond one process comes from partitioning the graph: each partition has its own allocator and graph, and a cross-partition reference is a (partition, NodeId) pair. A distributed graph needs that layer whatever the slot width.
- Scope guard: no work items and no design go down this goal's path beyond what Excel scope needs. The epic stays deferred. No bead adds Webs-specific abstractions, interfaces, APIs, workloads or extension slots, such as remote page access, a remote host transport, partition-aware IDs, DNA-only typed values or billion-node workloads, unless the owner places this epic. The notes on the attachment beads were narrowed to Excel-scope choices on the same day.

title: calc-func's x87 route has no wasm32 form: 15 Excel-bit tests fail in the browser
description:
## Outcome
calc-func's Excel-bit kernels give Excel's bits in the browser (wasm32) as they do on x86_64, so DNA OneCalc and DNA Calc in the browser publish the values Excel does.

## Found by
dc-msg, running calc-func's unit tests in Chrome and Firefox. `excel_numeric` reproduces Excel through the x87 CRT sequences (`x87.rs`, inline x87 assembly), which exist only on x86_64. On wasm32 every entry point takes its portable fallback (`powf`, `atan`, the glibc-2.29 exp/log port), which the module docs call "not bit-exact".

## Measured
In Chrome, 15 of calc-func's lib tests that pin live-Excel bits fail by one ULP (or by a count of pins), all through x87-route entry points: BINOM k=n and NEGBINOM k=0 (pow chain), BESSELY, BESSELJ, XNPV, PRICE, DURATION, POWER (fractional and negative-base reciprocal roots), T.INV.2T df=1 (tan), T.DIST df=2 pdf (pow chain), RRI (2 tests), NPER, NOMINAL. They are marked `Native-only:` with this bead named; `cargo xtask check --wasm` prints them per package.

## Do
- Give the x87 route a wasm32 form that reproduces the x86_64 bits (a software form of the x87 sequences the CRT runs, or of what Excel computes at these sites), measured against the x86_64 route over the pinned rows and a large sample.
- Then turn the 15 tests back to the native/browser attribute pair.
- dc-sbo (the `f64::powf` sites) is the neighbouring gap; the two may share a portable pow.
notes: Three more calc-func lib tests were already compiled only on x86_64 for the same reason (atan_retains_extended_inverse_angle_and_pi, gammaln stirling_ln87_dr_matches_current_build_hits_and_keeps_two_open, normal_dist_common phi_matches_live_excel_pinned_witnesses); dc-msg marks them `Native-only:` with this bead too, so 18 tests name dc-8dg.
close_reason: calc-func's Excel-bit kernels give Excel's bits in the browser: the x87 route has a software form (soft87.rs) that matches the hardware exactly for + - * /, sqrt, rounding, scaling, remainder and stores (0 differences in 100,000 random cases per operation under six control words; 0 in 400,000 double-rounded pairs), and runs each transcendental chain written once on hardware (x86_64) or in software (elsewhere), differing from the hardware in 0-85 per 1,000,000 random arguments per chain because the CPU microcode for F2XM1, FPTAN, FYL2X, FSIN, FCOS, FPATAN does not round exactly (no reproducible pattern found). Live-Excel witnesses in software: EXP 136 of 136, LN 95 of 113 (the 18 misses are 1 ulp and named by the test). 17 of the 18 tests that named dc-8dg run in Chrome and Firefox again. Evidence: cargo xtask check --wasm passed (calc-func 483 in both browsers, 16 native-only with reasons); catalogue oracle 5,998 of 6,309 identical cell for cell on the hardware and software routes (soft-x87 feature); Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272 on both routes. Commits 98046b0, f42ecc7. Still open: the microcode residue; platform libm calls (dc-ba bead filed alongside); software cost about 64 ns per arithmetic operation and 1-2.5 us per transcendental chain natively.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: Function exactness lane, 2026-10-25 (98046b0): the x87 chains run in the browser. excel_numeric/soft87.rs is the x87 in software (80-bit format; FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV/FSQRT/FRNDINT/FSCALE/FPREM1 and the binary64 store exact under every control word; ROM constants equal the hardware's; F2XM1/FYL2X/FPATAN/FSIN/FCOS/FPTAN round the exact value once). Each chain is written once over an Fpu trait: x86_64 runs the hardware, wasm32 the software x87 (feature soft-x87 runs it on x86_64 for measurement). Measured against the hardware (Ryzen 7 4800H): exact operations 0 differences in 100,000 per operation and control word; double-rounded + - * / and reciprocal 0 in 400,000 pairs each; binary64 chain results per 1,000,000 random arguments: EXP 0, ATAN reduced 0, staged SQRT 0, chopped EXP 1, SIN 3, COS 2, ATAN 3, BINOM exp 3, LOG10 9, LN 11, pow chain 13, TAN 16, GEOMEAN root 25, direct pow 85 (the residue is the hardware microcode: F2XM1 differs from the exactly rounded value at 3.3% of 64-bit results, FYL2X 2.1%, FPTAN 2.9%, FSIN 1.5%, FCOS 0.36%, FPATAN 0.11%). Live-Excel witnesses in software: EXP 136 of 136, LN 95 of 113 (18 named in the test, each a hardware FYL2X result that differs from the exactly rounded one). Catalogue oracle cell for cell identical on both routes (pass 5,998 of 6,309; fail 311 = 269 mismatched + 42 refused); Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272 on both. 17 of the 18 tests naming this bead run in Chrome and Firefox; BESSELY stays native-only for f64::ln (platform libm, dc-sbo). cargo xtask check --wasm: calc-func 481 in the browsers, 16 native-only. Still open: the microcode residue above. Not closed: the owner closes.

title: Keep infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency's OS-binding scenarios independent of the stand-in package's dependents
description:
## Outcome
infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency passes on a workspace in which portable packages depend on calc-value, because its OS-binding scenarios no longer depend on which packages happen to depend on the package that carries the stand-in crate.

## Context
Prerequisite of cfunc-m0.1's close (2026-10-15). cfunc-m0.1 adds calc-func's dependency on calc-value. The OS-binding scenarios of infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs, the `binding` table near line 1655) attach a stand-in `winapi` crate to crates/calc-value and expect exactly calc-value's lines. With the new edge, the check also reports, correctly, that portable calc-func has winapi in its wasm32-unknown-unknown closure, so os-binding-direct and os-binding-transitive each gain one line and the case fails ('failures: 2', round-3 refuter of cfunc-m0.1). The check is right; the expectation is too narrow. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask).

## Do
Attach the stand-in to a portable package that no workspace member may depend on, such as apps/dna-onecalc, or compute the expected lines from the copy's resolved metadata (the stand-in package plus each portable package whose closure reaches it). In either case, assert that every line the check prints names a package whose closure really contains the stand-in. Keep every other scenario of the case unchanged.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all
```
infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency passes on master after cfunc-m0.1's build commit, and its os-binding scenarios still fail when the deny-listed crate is present.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Changing the os-imports check itself.
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- The fix stays inside tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs; the os-imports check itself does not change.
- Attach the stand-in winapi and shim crates to apps/dna-onecalc, a portable package that no workspace member may depend on: a library or application depending on OneCalc would break plan 2.1's diagram. Then the expectation stays exactly one package's lines. Each scenario also asserts that every line the check prints names dna-onecalc, so a line about any other package fails the case.
- Proof: the case passes at HEAD 98f99fd (calc-func depends on calc-value) through `cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all`, and Linux runs after the push. The scenarios still fail when the deny-listed crate is present (the case asserts exit 1 and the exact lines).
close_reason:
Product status: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency passes again with calc-func depending on calc-value. Its OS-binding stand-in sits on apps/dna-onecalc, which no member depends on, and each scenario checks that from the copy's resolved metadata. The os-imports check is unchanged.
Evidence: commit 1416d1c, pushed after cfunc-m0.1's 98f99fd.
- Windows: cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all exit 0, "2 selected, 2 passed ... architecture checks 7/7 passed" (accept-receipts/infra-m0.3/windows.json).
- Linux, in the WSL clone at 1416d1c: cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all exit 0, "ACCEPT passed infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency" (accept-receipts/infra-m0.3/linux.json).
- fmt and clippy -D warnings exit 0.
- Probes failed the case when the check's wasm32 closure was emptied ("failures: 2") and when every line named calc-value ("failures: 4"). With the holder set to calc-value, the precondition and the resolved-metadata check also failed ("failures: 7"). Logs are under target/accept/dc-8gn8/.
- CI push run 38724812987 is green.
Still open: dc-tj29, for propagation between workspace members and native-only dependents. The "every line names the holder" assertion repeats the exact-lines and resolved-metadata assertions and protects nothing they miss.
