title: Language and engine cases dc-10y left refused
description:
## Outcome
The language and engine cases dc-10y left refused compute as Excel does.

## Context
dc-10y (bea7a7e) measured and implemented most of its list; these stay refused:
- OFFSET/INDIRECT lifted over an array returns an array of references: SUM adds them all, SUBTOTAL, N, SUMIF and COUNTIF lift element by element. Needs an array-of-references value.
- 3-D positions Excel's results do not settle (an IF branch not taken, criteria matching nothing), and functions nested under an array place (SUM inside SUMPRODUCT) at legacy single-value places.
- Typed entry: the number format Excel applies (date, percentage) is not set; a date without a year (host has no clock) and leading +/- text are refused.
- Cycle cells with iteration off whose only value is the file's stored one stay refused by rule (file caches never score); nothing to do unless the owner changes that rule.

Each item computes and matches captured Excel values, or is listed with what was tried.

title: Resolve _xlfn.-prefixed function names in a loaded formula to the catalogue function
description:
## Outcome
A formula loaded from a file that spells a function with Excel's file prefix (_xlfn.IFNA, _xlfn.MAXIFS, _xlfn._xlws.FILTER) compiles to the same catalogue function as its plain name, so calc_fml, calc_engine and calc_host compute it; the document keeps the file text unchanged, so a save writes the prefix back as loaded.

## Context
The first cargo xtask compare run (dc-kt3l, 2026-10-21): Default-tariff-cap-level spells IFNA as _xlfn.IFNA in 49 formulas whose results 62,786 other formula cells read, and calc_fml's compile refuses _xlfn.IFNA as UnknownFunction because it looks the spelling up as written (crates/calc-fml/src/eval/compile.rs). Every function Excel added after 2007 is stored with the prefix (MAXIFS, MINIFS, IFNA, XLOOKUP, CONCAT, FILTER), so loaded workbooks meet the same refusal. dc-552j owns the save half (adding prefixes to authored text from catalogue metadata) and converting UI text to file form; this bead takes only name resolution of the file form.

## Do
- In calc_fml's compile, resolve a call whose name carries the _xlfn. prefix, optionally followed by _xlws., by the name after the prefixes; keep the spelling as written for diagnostics; refuse as now when the plain name is not catalogued. Whether an unprefixed spelling of a prefixed function, or a prefixed spelling of a function Excel never prefixes, is accepted follows what Excel does when it loads such a file (measure it, or refuse with a typed refusal naming dc-552j).
- A case that compiles and evaluates =_xlfn.IFNA(...), =_xlfn.MAXIFS(...) (or catalogued functions that carry the prefix) through calc_fml::evaluate, and opens a generator-built package holding them through calc_host, with the cells calculated.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
_xlfn.-prefixed calls of catalogued functions compute through calc_fml::evaluate and through calc_host on a loaded package; an unknown prefixed name is still refused as UnknownFunction with its spelling.

## Out of scope
Adding prefixes on save, error constants on save, UI text conversion (dc-552j).

title: Adopt the MIT license for the DnaCalc workspace (DNA Kode, Inc.)
description:
## Outcome
The DnaCalc workspace is MIT-licensed, matching the legacy repositories. A root LICENSE names "Copyright (c) 2026 DNA Kode, Inc.", and every package declares license MIT, so that cargo metadata and every published bundle can state it.

## Context
Owner decisions (2026-10-18): the workspace license is MIT, matching the legacy repositories (OxFunc, OxFml, OxCalc and DnaTreeCalc are MIT), and the copyright holder is DNA Kode, Inc., as in DnaTreeCalc. The work prompt lists the license file as a wait, and this resolves it. Infrastructure files: the root LICENSE, [workspace.package] in Cargo.toml, the `license.workspace = true` line in each member's Cargo.toml, tools/xtask/ci-browser-fixture/Cargo.toml (its own workspace), tools/xtask's acceptance manifest and cases, and one AGENTS.md sentence.
Out of this bead:
- notices for third-party code and for ported legacy code in published bundles, which belong to the site beads dc-gh6q.8 and dc-gh6q.10;
- the license decisions per cited third-party algorithm source (glibc, fdlibm, SPECFUN) and for OxDoc, which belong to dc-4546.

## Do
- Add LICENSE at the repository root: the standard MIT text, word for word as in the legacy repositories' LICENSE files, with the line "Copyright (c) 2026 DNA Kode, Inc.".
- Set `license = "MIT"` in [workspace.package], and `license.workspace = true` in every member package, apps, platform and tools included. Set `license = "MIT"` in the separate ci-browser-fixture workspace.
- Add one AGENTS.md sentence: the workspace is MIT-licensed (LICENSE), and a new package inherits `license.workspace = true`.
- Add a named case that checks the result through cargo metadata and the LICENSE bytes, not through a flag.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-cyd7 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-cyd7 --platform linux --require-all
```
- `dc_cyd7__workspace_license`:
  - every package of `cargo metadata --no-deps` for the workspace and for tools/xtask/ci-browser-fixture reports license "MIT";
  - LICENSE equals the MIT template with the holder line "Copyright (c) 2026 DNA Kode, Inc.", byte for byte apart from line endings, and the template is taken from a legacy repository's LICENSE;
  - a fixture copy with one package's license removed fails the check;
  - `cargo xtask ci licenses` still passes.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Third-party and legacy-port notices in published bundles (dc-gh6q.8, dc-gh6q.10); per-source license decisions (dc-4546); relicensing any legacy repository.

title: DTC one-cell edit and memory against Excel; confirm Excel's CalculateFull timing
description:
## Outcome
DNA Calc's one-cell edit and its memory on the DTC model are no worse than Excel's, measured with cargo xtask bench; and Excel's own timings in the bench are shown to measure what they claim.

## Context
dc-10d9 (bdf33b3, C:\Work\DnaCalc\corpus\perf\final-bdf33b3\bench.md): DTC one-cell edit DNA 0.896 s vs Excel 0.222 s ('3g CPIH'!C328, 83,547 of 165,810 formulas recalculated); peak working set DNA 424 MB vs Excel 332 MB (about 230 MB of Excel's is an empty instance). Excel's CalculateFull measured 0.061 s on DTC, faster than its own one-cell edit (0.222 s) and 57x faster than its CalculateFullRebuild (3.481 s); that ordering is unexplained.

## Do
- First confirm the Excel figures: time CalculateFull with multithreaded calculation off on the script's own instance, check that every formula really recalculated (for example a volatile counter cell or CalculationState and a changed precedent), and record per-thread cost for both systems.
- Then cut DNA Calc's edit cost: reads of results the recalculation does not recompute (tree lookup), range reads through the cell walker, IF and SUM, the ready queue; and the INDIRECT reach on the benchmark sheets that widens the dirty set.
- Cut DTC peak memory.

## Acceptance
cargo xtask bench before/after medians on all three Ofgem workbooks; Ofgem stays 209,272 of 209,272.

title: Read digit-bearing text that cannot be a number, date or time as text, so labels such as 2016-17 Winter compute
description:
## Outcome
calc_func decides, for digit-bearing text that Excel's en-US number, date and time recognition cannot read (for example "2016-17 Winter" or "Q1 2016"), that it is not a number, so criteria, comparisons and coercions over such labels compute instead of being refused; text the rule cannot decide stays refused as not modelled.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b): refuter 2 of cfunc-m3.5 counted 1,748 criteria in Annex-4 built as "op"&cell over digit-bearing labels such as "2016-17 Winter". crates/calc-func/src/coerce.rs number_text refuses any text holding a digit outside the plain decimal form (owner NUMBER_TEXT, cfml-m2.6), and the conditional kernels refuse the call. cfml-m2.6 owns the whole number-text service (dates, times, fractions, currency, locales); this bead takes only the negative verdict that is certain.

## Do
- Measure in Excel on this machine which digit-bearing forms en-US Excel reads as numbers (VALUE over a generated list: month names and abbreviations, numeric dates with / and -, times with : and AM/PM, fractions, percent, currency, grouped digits, parenthesised negatives, exponents, weekday names), and write the rule from that: text holding a letter run that none of those forms accepts is not a number. Everything else outside the plain decimal form stays not modelled.
- Read-only scan of the three Ofgem workbooks (outside the repository, licence unverified: commit counts only, no cell text): the distinct digit-bearing texts in cells that criteria ranges cover and in the cells "op"&cell criteria name, and how many the rule decides.
- Narrow the NUMBER_TEXT owner in calc-func's acceptance tables to what still refuses; note on cfml-m2.6.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
Rows through calc_func::invoke (a comparison, a coercion such as "2016-17 Winter"+0, and a COUNTIF or SUMIF criterion over such labels): each decided row's result equals Excel's, measured on this machine and compared through calc_verdict once the capture route works (not_run with MissingCapture until then); undecided forms (a date with a month name, a time, a fraction) stay refused.

title: Prove the runner's wasm route runs real browsers
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask accept --platform wasm` records a case as passed in Chromium or Firefox only when that browser actually ran it, so cfunc-m0.1's wasm evidence is browser evidence and never a Node.js run.

## Context
Prerequisite of cfunc-m0.1, the first bead that declares wasm cases. Found by the infra-m0.3 refuters (2026-10-14): the wasm route sets only CARGO_TARGET_WASM32_UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN_RUNNER and CHROMEDRIVER or GECKODRIVER (tools/xtask/src/accept.rs:499-507); nothing forces a browser, and the outcome classifier never checks which browser ran (accept.rs:193-248). The excel and wasm not_run branches (Excel not registered, runner or driver missing; accept.rs:417-426, 464, 1016-1019) are exercised by no test. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask). Plan section 10.4: a wasm compile-only job is not browser validation.

## Do
Force browser execution for every wasm run and confirm from the runner's own output which browser executed each case; record that per browser in the receipt. Prove that `--list` and `--exact` select exactly one case under wasm-bindgen-test-runner. Add unit tests with an injected probe for each not_run branch (Excel absent, runner missing, driver missing). Install chromedriver matching the installed Chrome if the proof needs it, and name it in the commit message. Agents never run `--platform excel`.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform linux --require-all
```
- `dc_e8ql__browser_route` (registered under dc-e8ql in tools/xtask/acceptance.json, platforms windows and linux): a fixture wasm case that is not configured for a browser is recorded failed, never `<case>@chromium passed`; a fixture wasm case run in both browsers is recorded passed per browser with the browser's banner in its log; --list and --exact select exactly one case. On a host without the runner or drivers the case asserts the not_run outcome with its reason. Unit tests (`cargo test -p xtask --bins`) show each not_run branch with its reason.
## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution; the browser fixture runs on this Windows PC with Chrome and Firefox.

## Out of scope
CI (infra-m0.2); cfunc-m0.1's own cases.
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-14):
- Toolchain on this PC: Chrome 155.0.8059.40, Firefox 151.0.3, geckodriver 0.37.0 and wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.117 in %USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin. The orchestrator installed chromedriver 155.0.8059.39 there at claim, from Google's Chrome-for-Testing storage (the closest listed build of major version 155); the build commit names it. wasm-bindgen-test-runner requires the wasm-bindgen crate at exactly its own version, so the fixture pins wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and a matching wasm-bindgen-test. The WSL Ubuntu clone has no browser, driver or runner. Node.js is installed on both Windows and WSL, so an unconfigured wasm test can run under Node and must not be scored as a browser pass.
- This bead gets its own case, dc_e8ql__browser_route, registered in tools/xtask/acceptance.json under id dc-e8ql with platforms windows and linux. It holds the browser scenarios, and its receipts are accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/<platform>.json, so infra-m0.3's committed receipts stay as its close cites them. Acceptance: `cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform windows --require-all` and `--platform linux --require-all`.
- The case builds a fixture package with one wasm case in a temporary workspace copy, then runs `accept --id <fixture bead> --platform wasm --require-all` through the real runner. On a host with both drivers it must show three things. (1) Each browser recorded passed only when the runner's own output names that browser: a forced-browser setting (for example WASM_BINDGEN_USE_BROWSER), plus a check of the banner wasm-bindgen-test-runner prints ("Running headless tests in Chrome/Firefox" or the like). (2) A fixture case that is not configured for a browser is never recorded `<case>@chromium passed`. (3) --list and --exact select exactly one case under the runner. On a host without drivers (the WSL clone) the same scenario asserts the missing-driver not_run outcome, with its reason. The receipt states which branch ran, so the Linux pass proves the not_run branch, and only the Windows pass proves real browsers.
- Unit tests inject the probes for every not_run branch: Excel not registered, runner missing, and each driver missing.
- Agents never run --platform excel.
close_reason:
Product status: the runner's wasm route forces browser execution (WASM_BINDGEN_USE_BROWSER=1, the other browser's driver variables removed) and records a browser's run as passed only under that browser's own runner banner; a 1-passed Node.js run is failed. Per-browser receipt entries record browser, banner, driver environment and executed_in (format dnacalc-accept-receipt/4). chromedriver 155.0.8059.39 installed for Chrome 155.0.8059.40. Build commit 6e904a2, pushed.
Evidence: Windows (rustc/cargo 1.94.1, chromedriver 155.0.8059.39, geckodriver 0.37.0, wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.117), accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/windows.json: "ACCEPT passed dc_e8ql__browser_route (package xtask, exit code 0)", RESULT passed, architecture checks 6/6, exit code 0; its notes record branch browsers: fixture_browser__alpha@chromium passed under "Running headless tests in Chrome" with user agent HeadlessChrome/155, @firefox passed under "Running headless tests in Firefox" with user agent Firefox/151, fixture_browser_node__alpha reported 1 passed under Node.js/25 and was recorded failed in both browsers, and the pre-change route had run the same fixture under Node.js and reported it passed. cargo test -p xtask --bins 62 passed (each not_run branch), fmt, clippy -D warnings, infra_m0_1__agent_contract 1 passed, infra-m0.3 Windows regression passed (its receipt restored unchanged). Linux (WSL Ubuntu, rustc/cargo 1.93.1, clone at 6e904a2), accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/linux.json: dc_e8ql__browser_route passed, RESULT passed, exit code 0, branch not_run (wasm-bindgen-test-runner not on PATH, so no real browser is proven on Linux; the driver-missing branch with a runner present is unit-tested only).
Still open: dc-pih5 (driver variables, banner position, versions in receipts, pinned fixture lock, driver-missing scenario with a runner present).

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text:
2026-10-27 (DnaCalc-ceng): candidate public corpora for V2, from the sources' own pages (nothing downloaded). Licence as each source states it; sizes as listed. Format matters: calc-doc reads OOXML (.xlsx/.xlsm) only, so a .xls (BIFF) corpus needs each file converted by Excel (open, SaveAs .xlsx) before capture, which changes the file and adds a capture step.
1. Sheetpedia, xlsx edition: https://huggingface.co/datasets/tianzl66/Sheetpedia_xlsx (paper: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks, "Sheetpedia: A 300K-Spreadsheet Corpus"). Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (dataset card). 211,326 rows, 3.69 GB, .xlsx inside .tar.gz shards. Draws on Enron, FUSE and a crawl of Excel forums; already .xlsx, so no conversion. Adds: the largest formula-bearing set in OOXML, forum workbooks (formula-heavy, varied functions). Suggested first request: a sample of a few hundred to a few thousand files from one or two shards.
2. Enron spreadsheets (Hermans and Murphy-Hill 2015): https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.1221767 (figshare item "Enron Spreadsheets and Emails"). Licence: CC BY 4.0 (figshare metadata). spreadsheets.7z, 992,635,888 bytes (the emails are separate, 13 parts of about 734 MB, not needed). 15,770 spreadsheets, 9,120 with formulas; mostly .xls (BIFF), some in older formats. Adds: real business models (energy trading, finance), heavy on SUM/IF/VLOOKUP, dates and financial functions; needs .xls conversion.
3. VEnron (Dou et al., versioned Enron spreadsheets): 7,294 spreadsheets in 360 evolution groups, a subset of the Enron set; licence not found on the pages read. Adds: versions of one workbook, useful for edit and recalculation scenarios rather than function coverage. Would follow from item 2.
4. FUSE (Barik et al., MSR 2015): https://zenodo.org/record/581678. Licence: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo). fuse.zip, 9.4 GB, 249,376 spreadsheets extracted from Common Crawl, with JSON metadata (formula counts and functions per file), so a formula-dense subset can be chosen before download. Formats not stated (mostly .xls by the paper). Adds: breadth of web spreadsheets; needs .xls conversion for most.
5. EUSES (Fisher and Rothermel 2005): original at eusesconsortium.org (site linked from TU Graz); 4,498 spreadsheets from the web, mostly .xls; licence not stated on the pages read. TU Graz offers a modified EUSES (576 single-fault versions; cite Hofer et al. FASE 2013), licence not stated. Adds: a classic benchmark set; low formula density; licence needs confirmation with the source.
6. Apache POI test-data (spreadsheet folder): https://github.com/apache/poi/tree/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet. Licence: Apache 2.0 (the project). About 343 files, about 69% .xls and 24% .xlsx/.xlsm, including formula-evaluation fixtures (FormulaEvalTestData_Copy.xlsx, IndexFunctionTestCaseData.xls, IrrNpvTestCaseData.xls, LookupFunctionsTestCaseData.xls, countifExamples.xls, yearfracExamples.xls). Adds: edge cases chosen to test formula evaluation and file-format corners; small (tens of MB).
7. LibreOffice core spreadsheet test data: https://git.libreoffice.org/core/+/refs/heads/master/sc/qa/unit/data (also GitHub mirror). Licence: MPL 2.0 (the project). Many .xlsx/.xls/.ods files including per-category function tests (functions/ tests of statistical, text, database and other functions). Adds: function coverage with expected values written by another implementation's QA; .xlsx files usable directly, .ods not.
8. UK regulator and government models (Open Government Licence v3.0 where the site states it; ONS states OGL v3.0 for its dataset pages): Ofgem's other price-cap period models (Annex 9 levelised rates about 1.3 MB, pre-levelised rates about 5 MB per period) at https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/energy-policy-and-regulation/policy-and-regulatory-programmes/energy-price-cap-default-tariff-policy/energy-price-cap-default-tariff-levels; Ofwat PR24 financial and bill waterfall models (.xlsm) at https://www.ofwat.gov.uk/publication/pr24-bill-waterfall-model/ (licence not confirmed on the pages read: Ofwat's page refused the fetch); ONS datasets (mostly data, few formulas; .xls/.csv). Adds: large regulator models like the Ofgem one already in V1 (deep formula chains, financial functions), at a few to tens of workbooks.
Recommendation: request (a) the Apache POI and LibreOffice test-data folders (small, permissive, formula-focused), (b) a sample of Sheetpedia_xlsx shards (CC BY-SA 4.0, already .xlsx), and (c) the other Ofgem price-cap period models; Enron/FUSE after deciding on .xls conversion through Excel.

comments.text:
2026-10-27 (DnaCalc-ceng), dc-ebb candidates, checked against the repositories' own listings (no download):
- Apache POI: https://github.com/apache/poi/tree/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet exists on trunk (the earlier count of 343 files, 69% .xls and 24% .xlsx/.xlsm, came from the googlesource mirror's excelant branch; GitHub lists 100+ names before "View all files"). title: LEN of text a file holds beyond 32,767 code units
description: dc-ifc's local corpus (STR8-041, 2 workbooks): a cell whose file text is 32,773 UTF-16 units (16,383 emoji then 7 letters) gives LEN 32,767 in Excel and 16,383 in DNA Calc. title: Report the calculation context HostState recalculates under
description:
## Outcome
calc_host reports the calculation context its recalculation applies (date system, iteration, precision as displayed), so a comparison derives the run's context fingerprint from the product, not from the capture or a constant.

## Context
Design of the real-workbook comparison (2026-10-21): calc-doc does not read calcPr, so HostState always recalculates in the 1900 date system, without iteration and at full precision. dc-qguw's round-2 judge note on infra-m1.3 asks that the record's context come from the run. ceng-m4.3 carries calcPr into the engine later and changes these values.

## Do
- A HostState accessor returning a plain struct (date1904, iteration, precision_as_displayed), with no enum variants nothing produces.
- Document that ceng-m4.3 changes the values; note on chost-m1.2.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
```
A generator-built package declaring date1904="1", iterate="1" and fullPrecision="0" opens through HostState::open and reports date1904=false, iteration=false and precision_as_displayed=false (what the host applies), and the case says which of them the package declared.

## Out of scope
Reading calcPr (ceng-m4.3).
notes:

title: Evaluate IFERROR and IFNA lazily through calc_fml, ahead of LET and LAMBDA
description:
## Outcome
IFERROR and IFNA evaluate through calc_fml::evaluate and the catalogue: the value argument first, the fallback only when the value is an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA), with the array-context behaviour Excel documents.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison census (2026-10-21) finds IFERROR in the formulas of 19,648 cells of three real regulatory models, the largest single function blocker, and IFNA in 49. IFERROR sits in cfml-m2.4 (lazy control forms), which waits on cfml-m2.3 (LET and LAMBDA closures); IFERROR and IFNA need neither. IF already evaluates through the catalogue's BranchOnCondition demand (cfml-m1.3). This bead takes IFERROR and IFNA out of cfml-m2.4 (and IFNA out of cfunc-m3.21) so they land now.

## Do
- Catalogue entries for IFERROR and IFNA with a lazy argument demand, and calc-fml evaluation that evaluates the fallback only on an error; an error held in a reference or array argument follows Microsoft's pages.
- Cases with hand-derived values labelled documented or unmeasured, and the rows in an oracle workbook for an Excel capture; agents may run Excel on this machine (AGENTS.md), so capture it and compare.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform excel --require-all
```
IFERROR(1/0,5) is 5, IFERROR(2,1/0) is 2 without evaluating 1/0, IFNA(#N/A,1) is 1, IFNA(#DIV/0!,1) is #DIV/0!, and every row matches the Excel capture.

## Out of scope
IFS, SWITCH, CHOOSE (cfml-m2.4).
notes:
Claimed 2026-10-21 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cfml. IFERROR is the single largest function blocker in the three Ofgem price-cap models the owner chose for the Excel comparison (19,648 formula cells call it).
- Port: look up every OxFunc and OxFml file you would read for IFERROR and IFNA (surface_dispatch.rs entries, their kernels and tests, OxFml's lazy-argument scheduling) with `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup`; port only exit 0 (exit 6 only against clean replacements); exit 5 or 3 is not read and the behaviour is written fresh from Microsoft's pages. Record each lookup and its exit in migration/ports/dc-ibp2.json.
- The capability to show, through calc_fml::evaluate (and calc_func's catalogue, which resolves the names):
  - IFERROR(value, value_if_error) and IFNA(value, value_if_na) evaluate value first and evaluate the fallback only when value is an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA); otherwise the fallback is never evaluated (show it: a fallback whose evaluation would be observed, for example through the ReadObserver or a refused call, is not reached).
  - An empty value is 0 as Excel's pages say (check what they say), and a value or fallback that is a reference is read as the pages say; an array or a range in an array context follows the pages or is refused with a typed not-modelled refusal (array lifting belongs to cfml-m3.4).
  - Reuse the lazy demand IF already uses (catalogue ArgumentDemand, calc-fml's branch evaluation) or extend it additively; do not add a second evaluation path.
- Cases: dc_ibp2__error_fallback (IFERROR and IFNA over values, errors of every kind, references to error cells and to cells holding values, nested inside arithmetic, and the not-evaluated fallback) with each row's expected value labelled documented or unmeasured choice, and an oracle workbook of these rows from a committed generator. Agents may run Excel on this machine (AGENTS.md, 'Excel on this machine'): capture that workbook with `cargo xtask capture` and add a comparison case that judges every row against the capture through calc_verdict, as cfunc-m1.2's comparison does, so the bead closes on measured agreement.
- Keep calc_fml's and calc_func's public signatures unchanged or extend them additively.
- What green does not show: IFS, SWITCH and CHOOSE (cfml-m2.4).
close_reason: Product status: IFERROR and IFNA evaluate through calc_fml::evaluate and calc-func's catalogue (family 8, crates/calc-func/src/catalogue/error_fallback.rs) with the lazy demand ArgumentDemand::FallbackOnError: the value first, the fallback only on an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA). IFERROR(1/0,5) is 5; IFERROR(2,1/0) is 2 without running 1/0; IFNA(#N/A,1) is 1; IFNA(#DIV/0!,1) is #DIV/0!; the package form =_xlfn.IFNA(#N/A,1) gives 1 (with dc-besk). An empty root value is published as 0 for every formula, as Excel's capture shows. Against Excel 16.0.20430.20182's capture of the oracle workbook, through calc_verdict::judge: calculated 74 of 83 formula cells, matched 74 of 74 calculated, 0 mismatched; 6 conditional rows over the FILTER, SEQUENCE and FIELDVALUE sources not modelled (each agrees with Excel given the source cell's value) and the 3 sources not modelled; 0 strict-bit certified (Fast policy; 1 COM add-in connected); 1 reopen-stage capture failure (D13 =IFNA(#GETTING_DATA,1)) reported, not compared. Excel's own laziness is not measured. Evidence: build commit 7b59bf6; cargo xtask accept --id dc-ibp2 --platform windows --require-all (started 2026-10-21T15:31:52Z), --platform wasm (15:30:09Z, Chrome and Firefox) and --platform excel (15:31:11Z, live capture matched 74 of 74), each exit 0 with 2/2, 2/2 and 1/1 passed, at fce24e6 plus the diff that became 7b59bf6; --platform linux in the WSL clone of 7b59bf6 (started 15:51:07Z, clean tree): 2 selected, 2 passed, exit 0. title: Excel's exact bits in the ported function kernels (distributions, regression, financial solvers)
description:
## Outcome
The statistical distribution and regression functions ported from OxFunc return Excel's exact binary64 results, not values 1-4 ulp away.

## Context
F1 (dc-8dq, 2026-10-23) ported OxFunc's kernels. In the catalogue oracle (crates/calc-func/tests/fixtures/catalogue), 59 cells mismatch Excel by 1-4 ulp (IMSEC by a 15th-digit text): t distribution 12 (T.DIST family, T.INV.2T, TINV, T.TEST, CONFIDENCE.T), discrete pmf 9 (BINOM/HYPGEOM/NEGBINOM), regression 8 (LINEST, LOGEST, TREND, GROWTH; a one-predictor TREND is exact in Excel), F distribution 7, beta 6, gamma 6, normal inverse 6, chi-squared 4, IMSEC 1. Cheap reorderings did not reproduce Excel's bits.

## Do
Find Excel's algorithm per root cause (series, continued fractions, QR vs normal equations, final rounding) from more captured rows, and match it. One root cause at a time, each fix shown on the catalogue oracle.

## Acceptance
The catalogue oracle's mismatches in these functions go to 0, or the rest are listed with what was tried.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text:
2026-10-27 (DnaCalc-ceng): annuity family (409 of the 539 mismatches), one time-boxed round, not fixed; measurements for the next attempt:
- PMT(r,n,pv) = RN(pv*Q) for one real Q per (r,n) over 60 pv values (r=0.2, n=300): PMT is one pv-proportional chain.
- PPMT is none of RN(PMT*V), RN(pv*W), RN(RN(pv*Q')*V) for any real V, W, Q' (same 60 pv values, k=100): pv enters PPMT through more than one rounding.
- Along one annuity (r=0.2, n=300, pv=1000, k=1..300) Excel's PPMT relative to PMT*(1+r)^-m (m=n-k+1, exact, Excel's PMT) is above it, growing sawtooth with m to 64 units of 2^-53 at m=231; PMT*exp(RN(-m*(log1p(r) - 1 ulp))) fits 185 of 300 (log1p(r) itself 16), and 10 of 12 at r=0.05/12.
- 295 random PPMT readings: best chain is PMT*exp(RN(-m*log1p r)) (134); tried and worse: x87 exp, FYL2XP1 or extended m*log1p into the fFEXP tail (with and without an extended product), (1+r)^-m via the CRT pow, Excel's POWER kernel, pow chains, two powers (1+r)^(k-1)/(1+r)^n, Kahan log1p with x87 ln, log space (exp(ln|PMT|-mL)). For most misses no binary64 exponent t within 60 ulp gives PMT*exp(t) = Excel's value.
- At k = n Excel's PPMT is within 1 ulp of PMT/(1+r); at k = 1, 2 the misses grow with m.
GEOMEAN (38): current chain (binary64 product, 2^(log2(p)/n) in the x87 registers) 184 of 220; tried and worse: Excel's POWER kernel, exp of the mean ln (x87 and CR), sum of FYL2X in extended, extended product, stored exponent, FYL2X(1/n,p). Excel's value is up to 1.4 ulp from the exact geometric mean and up to 1.3 ulp from the exact root of the binary64 product.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text:
2026-10-27 (DnaCalc-ceng), next round, no code change; constraints recorded.
LINEST through INDEX (25): no lifting or selection error; all are numeric. The two large ones (rows 1796, 1811: LINEST/LOGEST over {1;2;4;7} with X columns x and 2x+0.0001, the constant's standard error, relative 1.5e-7) come from our constant-variance formula w'(R'R)^-1 w, which cancels on near-collinear data: exact 0.21066252211737, Excel 0.21066252128034, ours 0.21066248860646, an uncentred Householder QR of [1|X] 0.21066252211091, a centred one 0.21066251710691. Solving R'z = w by forward substitution fixes 8 of the 1-ulp cells and breaks 5 others (net +3), so it is not Excel's algorithm either; not adopted. The 10-observation set (rows 1094-1104, 2 to 10 ulp) and the 1-ulp cells need Excel's exact QR sequence.
Distribution and solver cells (67): each is its own kernel; relative to the exact value Excel is sometimes nearer (T.DIST.RT(1.96,60): Excel 13 ulp from exact, ours 2; GAMMA.DIST pdf: Excel exact, ours 3 ulp off; BINOM.DIST(6,10,0.5): Excel +2, ours -2) and sometimes farther. RATE/IRR/YIELD/ODDFYIELD differ by 1e2 to 2e6 ulp: Excel iterates to full convergence (RATE(48,-200,8000): Excel within 2e-16 of the root; ours stops at |f| <= 1e-7, 2e-13 away); matching their bits needs Excel's exact iteration function.
PPMT, black-box isolation with dyadic rates (1+r exact; pv=1024; per=1, 2 and nper; 8 rates x 12 nper; 624 readings):
- PMT is within 2 ulp of exact (59 of 96 exact).
- PPMT(nper,nper) (one period of discount) equals RN(PMT*RN(exp(-log1p r))) in 81 of 96; for r=0.375 the discount that fits alternates between RN(1/(1+r)) - 1 and + 1 ulp as nper changes, so the discount is not a function of r alone; for r=0.75 no binary64 discount fits.
- IPMT(1) is off by 1 ulp from the exact -pv*r (representable here) in 20 of 88: IPMT(1) is not computed as -pv*r.
- In Excel's own readings IPMT = RN(PMT - PPMT) holds in 61 of 88 at per=1, 52 of 80 at per=2, 25 of 96 at per=nper; PPMT = RN(PMT - IPMT) in 28, 27 and 60. Neither identity holds throughout, so both come from a common unrounded quantity or from different formulas by period.
- PPMT(per,nper) = -pv*r*(1+r)^(per-1)/((1+r)^nper - 1) through x87 exp and Excel's expm1 matches 30 to 39 of 295 random readings: not Excel's form.
GEOMEAN, isolated with integer arguments whose product is exact in binary64 (211 of 300 readings): the root chain alone differs: Excel is correctly rounded in 181 and 1 ulp off in 30, where the exact root lies 0.16 to 0.5 ulp from the correctly rounded value; our extended chain is correctly rounded throughout. Rounding the fraction f of the exponent to binary64 before F2XM1 gives 186 of 211; rounding w or m, a stored log2, 1/n as a binary64 multiplier, and FYL2X(1/n,P) do not fit.

title: D2b: insert and delete rows and columns through calc-host, with undo and save
description: Structural edits as host intents: insert/delete rows and columns on a sheet, one undo step each. References adjust as Excel's do (including #REF! for deleted targets, ranges that grow and shrink, other sheets, defined names, spill anchors); formats, column widths, row heights and hidden bands move with the edit; the save writes moved rows and columns so Excel opens the file without repair and every saved value equals Excel's recalculation. Accept: tests against Excel-captured results of the same insert/delete sequences, the differential session test extended with structural steps, an Ofgem round trip with an insert and a delete per workbook. DNA Calc (dc-09v) uses these intents for its insert/delete commands.
close_reason: Insert and delete rows and columns are calc-host intents (SkinIntent::EditAxis), one undo step each, with redo. References adjust as Excel's do (#REF! for deleted targets, ranges grow and shrink, other sheets and defined names follow); spill anchors, tables, hidden bands, number formats, heights and widths move; edits Excel refuses (splitting a legacy array, table header/totals/columns, pushing cells off the grid) are refused with typed errors. The save writes moved rows and columns with merges, conditional formats, validations (including extension-list ones), hyperlinks, filters and sorts, page breaks, views, comments, notes, threaded comments, drawing anchors and tables; chart formulas and defined names are rewritten; pivot caches, scenarios, OLE objects and controls naming edited cells are refused (SaveRefusal::StructuralNotMoved). Evidence: an Excel fixture of 8 edits on 3 sheets matches Excel's own edits on inputs, names, formats, sizes and all 15 values, through undo-all/redo-all and save/reopen, and Excel opens the save without repair; a random session test (29 structural steps, 49 saves); Ofgem round trip with one insert and one delete per workbook (crates/calc-host/tests/fixtures/d2/ofgem-structural-round-trip.json): Annex 4 10,580/10,580, Annex 9 32,880/32,880, default tariff cap 165,780/165,780 formulas equal to Excel's own edit and to Excel's capture, all inputs equal. The comparison script skips row heights Excel recomputes on save (non-custom heights). Commits f34979f, 6012758, d123bfd, e6bda39. Still open: an inserted row's outline level and conditional-format coverage not measured against Excel; charts on an edited sheet are rewritten but not in any Ofgem file; pivots refused.

title: Retire the legacy source repositories of the DNA Calc rework
description: Owner direction 2026-10-27: do the extra work to retire OxFunc, OxFml, OxCalc, OxDoc, OxReplay, OxXlPlay, DnaTreeCalc and DnaOneCalc. Retire means: every item in parked/assess/*.md for that repository is done or recorded, its legacy tests are reviewed under the test migration plan, its local-only content is evaluated, and then its GitHub repository is archived read-only (the archive stays, because DNA Calc cites these repositories by commit). title: Clock-dependent cells compare against Excel's calculation time
description: dc-ifc's local corpus: 9 cells in 6 workbooks are NOW() or read it (INDEX, VALUETOTEXT); they mismatch by seconds because DNA Calc's clock is the capture's calculation_clock (local time when the worker started), not the instant Excel's calculation read. Decide and implement how a capture records and the verdict judges a value that depends on the clock (record Excel's own NOW at calculation in the capture, or class such cells as clock-dependent), then re-run the corpus. Accept: no clock-dependent cell counts as a mismatch for a difference of the calculation instant alone, and the rule is stated in the verdict.

title: Compare a workbook's DNA Calc calculation with its Excel capture, cell by cell, and classify every difference
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask compare --fixture <xlsx> --capture <capture.json> --out <dir> [--exact-target ...]` opens a real workbook through calc_host (HostState::open, step with an unlimited budget, project), judges every formula cell of the capture's inventory with calc_verdict::judge against an evaluation record built from the evaluator's own reports, and writes report.json, evaluations.json and triage.json, with a one-screen summary: inventory, calculated, matched, mismatched by class, not modelled by root key with the cells each root blocks.

## Context
The owner (2026-10-21): compare DNA Calc with Windows Excel on real workbooks on this machine to guide development, correctness first, then performance. The Excel capture adapter (infra-m1.2) records every formula cell of a workbook after a full rebuild; nothing on the DNA side yet evaluates a whole workbook into a result set. This bead is the only product writer of the evaluation record (infra-m1.3 builds on it; one verdict feed, AGENTS.md).

## Do
1. Refuse unless sha256 of the bytes equals the capture's source.
2. HostState::open; on OpenFailure every inventory cell is missing with the typed error.
3. step with a ReadObserver recording evaluated reports, calls and read areas; drop all evaluations when step fails.
4. Project exactly the inventory cells; map ProjectedValue onto calc-verdict's Provenance (Calculated with the context from the context-report bead, FileCached, Stale, NotModeled with its typed refusal, Empty or Literal as missing).
5. Judge in-process; write the report and the InstrumentRecord.
6. Triage: each inventory cell gets exactly one class (capture, doc, engine, context, formula, function-missing, kernel-value or kernel-bits, matched) and a key (the typed refusal, the function spelling, the LoadError variant), with root cells and cells blocked only because they read a root kept apart. A difference in a calc-func kernel's result is classed kernel-value or kernel-bits with the FunctionId, the argument values the reads show, both results' bits, the ulp distance and agreement to 15 significant digits.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform excel --require-all
```
<bead>__every_cell_classified (windows): a generator-built workbook and a capture authored in the test with hand-derived Excel values (labelled as such) holding a SUM chain, a deliberately wrong formula cache, a not-modelled function and a reader of it: every inventory cell gets one class, and the wrong cache never scores. <bead>__live_capture (excel): the same workbook captured live on this machine and compared.

## Out of scope
Fixing what the triage finds (the Ofgem comparison bead files it).
close_reason: Closed in the bulk-port redirect (2026-10-23): built code on master with passing receipts; cargo xtask check passed on Windows for all 13 packages at 99edc1b. Remaining gaps belong to the work packages in docs/plan/BULK_PORT_PLAN.md.

title: Let the context fingerprint ignore iteration limits while iteration is off
description:
## Outcome
calc_verdict's context fingerprint depends on the iteration limits only while iteration is on, and a caller can build a context without iteration limits, so a run whose host applies no iteration derives the whole fingerprint from its own context.

## Context
dc-hqcv's round-1 judge (2026-10-21): CalculationContext::fingerprint (tools/calc-verdict/src/session.rs) always formats max_iterations and max_change, which HostState's applied context cannot supply (the host applies no iteration), so `cargo xtask compare` (dc-kt3l) would have to take them from the capture or a constant. With iteration off the limits change no value; the capture worker forces 100 and 0.001 then.

## Do
- With iteration off, fingerprint() names Excel's default limits (100 and 0.001) whatever the context holds, so captures taken with iteration off keep their fingerprint.
- CalculationContext::without_iteration(date1904, precision_as_displayed).
- A unit test: two contexts with iteration off and different limits have one fingerprint; with iteration on they differ.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform windows --require-all
```
The unit test passes, and every existing capture and evaluation fixture keeps its fingerprint.

## Out of scope
Iterative calculation (ceng-m5.2).
close_reason: Built in d6cc2c2 (calc-verdict): CalculationContext::fingerprint names Excel default iteration limits (100, 0.001) while iteration is off, and CalculationContext::without_iteration(date1904, precision_as_displayed) builds such a context. capture_v2_tests::the_calculation_context_fingerprint_names_every_setting shows the string for iteration off with the defaults is unchanged, three other limit pairs leave it unchanged while iteration is off and change it while iteration is on. Windows: cargo test -p calc-verdict --lib 40 passed; infra-m1.1 windows and wasm and dc-qguw windows passed. Linux in WSL at 4922f25: calc-verdict lib 40 passed, infra-m1.1 and dc-qguw linux passed. A read-only reviewer checked every producer and consumer of the string before the push. dc-hqcv adds the first non-test caller.

title: Derive infra-m0.5's tainted-commit list by rule, check it at accept time, and review ffcb9a77
description:
## Outcome
migration/numeric-provenance.json's tainted_commits list is derived from a rule the record states, the infra-m0.5 case recomputes it from `git log` at the pinned commit and fails when a commit is missing, and an independent reviewer's verdict on OxFunc commit ffcb9a77 is recorded by that reviewer, so infra-m0.5 can close.

## Context
Prerequisite of infra-m0.5, holding its close (2026-10-15). infra-m0.5's round-3 judge left two blocking findings after the third implementer round: (1) the tainted-commit list was hand-picked (16 commits) while the record's own reasons name a class (W108/W109 identification commits) that `git log -i -E --grep='W10[89].*identif|identif.*(graph|staging)|IDENTIFIED' 6fca3518` finds 64 of, and the case only checks that five named commits are present (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_5.rs:1216-1235); (2) the implementer alone decided not to list ffcb9a77, which modified excel_numeric/x87.rs and mod.rs and added smart-fuzzer/tools/w111/complex_kernel_probe (a tainted class) as well as the W111 captures. As a conservative data fix the orchestrator listed every commit matching the stated rule (identification commits, and every commit whose message holds one of the record's 15 sweep patterns: 70 commits) plus ffcb9a77, pending this bead. Infrastructure files only. The infra-m0.5 reading rule applies.

## Do
State the derivation rule in the record and make `cargo xtask pin-sources` and the accept-time check derive the list from git at the pin, failing on any omission; run an independent review (a separate reviewer agent, its verbatim output committed) of ffcb9a77 and of every commit the rule adds, with witness independence argued from the capture files' own acquisition, not from a commit being unlisted; apply the verdicts; remove from both migration files the remaining staging residue (the 87disp control-word value and the helper instruction sequences quoted at numeric-provenance.json:76, 130-141, 163, 343-344, and the staging tokens listed in infra_m0_5.rs:68, 1814), keeping only citing clauses; settle the disposition of extended-numeric/numeric-outcomes.json and check, rather than assert, that it was written before the freeze steps.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.5 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.5 --platform linux --require-all
```
A fixture in which the record omits a commit the rule finds makes infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate fail; `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` exits 5 for OxFunc functions/combin.rs, combina.rs, matrix_family.rs, misc_conversion_family.rs, regression_forecast_family.rs, beta_gamma_stats_family.rs, chi_f_t_family.rs, statistical_tests_family.rs, asin.rs, acot.rs and atan.rs unless a reviewed per-file entry clears one; the review file holds the reviewer's ffcb9a77 verdict.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Clearing any catalogue file (dc-2203).
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- Order: an independent review first, then the implementer round. The review is a separate, read-only reviewer agent whose verbatim structured output is committed as migration/numeric-provenance-review-2026-10-15-commits.json. It gives a verdict on ffcb9a77 and on each of the 55 commits the stated rule added. For every file the witness chain depends on, it says whether that file's own acquisition evidence shows black-box Excel capture independent of the tainted research that ffcb9a77 also carries: the five answer captures, extended-numeric/numeric-outcomes.json and its writer retain_numeric_campaign.py, the runner Run-W109BulkBatch.ps1 at the blob that ran, CellRefBatch.psm1, run_numeric_campaign.py, the input generator, and the snapshot and freeze scripts. It also checks the ordering claim, that the retention was written before the freeze steps.
- Precedence change: a file changed by a listed tainted commit stays at least unresolved unless a reviewed per-file entry clears it and names that commit as considered. The witness chain is admitted only through such entries.
- The tainted-commit list is derived by the stated rule (W108/W109 identification commits, plus commits whose message holds a sweep pattern), plus the commits the review ties to the pass. Both `cargo xtask pin-sources` and the accept-time check recompute it from `git log` at the pin and fail on any omission.- Review done (2026-10-15, workflow run wf_5ba77a06-ea9; saved verbatim as migration/numeric-provenance-review-2026-10-15-commits.json). The 55 rule-added commits: 22 tainted, 24 unresolved, 9 not_tied_to_pass. ffcb9a77: tainted. All 15 witness-chain files are cleared on their own acquisition evidence, or as having supplied no bits. Retention-before-freeze: not established, so witness independence rests on hash continuity. The reviewer reported reading_rule_kept=false and disclosed incidental reads of script code beyond docstrings; it read no x87 body.
Rulings after round 1 (2026-10-15, orchestrator): (a) Names used as labels in a citing clause are citations, not staging, and may stay: an instruction mnemonic such as F2XM1 or FYL2X, a chain label such as fFEXP, or a symbol name such as excel_x87_mul. What must not appear is a staging formula, an instruction sequence, a control-word value or a code line. The verbatim commits review stays as written. (b) Four witness-independence limits are owned by dc-z5ay (its notes now name them). (c) The work done here is recorded on dc-qfqa and dc-2203.
Rulings after round 2 (2026-10-15, orchestrator): (a) The infra-m0.4 Windows regression compares against HEAD's committed manifest, so the orchestrator runs it after the build commit; infra-m0.4's Linux run on the pushed commit, with its committed receipt, also comes with this bead's close. (b) Round 3 limits the acquisition lifting of the tainted-commit rule to files that supply expected bits (the five answer captures and the retention). Scripts the review cleared only for their witness-chain role keep the provenance the content rules give them for porting, so their `--lookup` must not read as clean port inputs. (c) Code-line quotes are not allowed even when they carry no staging content (ruling (a) of round 1). The gen_tables.py PROBE path assignment and the excel_bond_pow signature line become citing clauses. (d) The remaining round-2 follow-ups belong to dc-qfqa (its notes list them), and dc-1c6a now depends on dc-qfqa.
Ruling after round 3 (2026-10-15, orchestrator): Cargo.toml lines that name features only, for example features = ["research-x87"], are configuration quotes and may stay. Ruling (c) applies to code that could carry derived content. The round-3 follow-ups are recorded on dc-qfqa.

title: independent_lanes: leave cargo's last-use tracker out of the shared cargo-home check
description:
## Outcome
infra_m0_1__independent_lanes passes or fails on what the four lane builds do, not on cargo's own bookkeeping: an update of cargo's last-use tracker in the shared cargo home is not reported as a lane writing shared state.

## Context
2026-10-21, on master 60c338d with a clean tree: `cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all` failed once with 'the lane builds changed the shared cargo home C:\Users\GovertvanDrimmelen\.cargo: [".global-cache"]' (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance.rs, the case's cargo-home comparison), and passed on the next run of the same commit. .global-cache is the SQLite database in which cargo records when each cached registry crate was last used; cargo refreshes those times only when they are older than its update interval, so whether a build writes it depends on when the crates were last used, not on the lane's behaviour. Other cargo processes on the machine (lane clones building at the same time) can also write it.

## Do
- Leave .global-cache (and its -wal/-shm companions, if present) out of the cargo-home comparison, and say why in the case's evidence; or show that a lane's own build wrote it and report that separately from a lane writing anything else.
- Keep every other path of the cargo home compared.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
A probe that touches .global-cache during the lane builds leaves the case green with an evidence line naming it; a probe that writes any other file under the cargo home turns it red.

## Out of scope
Changing cargo's own garbage-collection settings.

title: Give a number's text as Excel gives it when & or a function reads the number as text
description:
## Outcome
calc_func gives a number's text as Excel gives it when an operator or a function reads the number as text (the & operator first), so formulas such as A1&"-"&B1 or "="&D$145 over a number compute instead of being refused as not modelled.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b): 1,402 cells of the three price-cap workbooks use &, and refuter 2 of cfunc-m3.5 counted 1,472 criteria in Annex-4 built as "op"&cell over a number. crates/calc-func/src/coerce.rs `text` refuses every number (owner GENERAL_TEXT, cfml-m2.6). cfml-m2.6 is the whole number-format service (TEXT, cell display, locales); this bead takes only the conversion a number gets when it is read as text, in en-US, with no column width. cfml-m2.6's service later takes it over unchanged.

## Do
- Implement the conversion in calc-func's coerce module (the only site today) for every finite binary64: up to 15 significant digits, the switch to E notation and its exact form (E+15, E-07, mantissa digits), negative numbers and negative zero, as Excel gives them. Port from OxFunc where `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` exits 0 for the file read; otherwise write it from measurement.
- Measure the rows in Excel on this machine (agents may run Excel; see AGENTS.md): an oracle workbook from the committed generator, its rows compared through calc_verdict once `cargo xtask capture` works; until then the comparison case is not_run with MissingCapture and every row's expected text is labelled with how it was obtained.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
Rows through calc_func::invoke of & with a number: integers up to and past 15 digits, the boundaries around 1E+15 and 1E+21, small numbers from 1E-4 to 1E-10, sums whose 16th and 17th digits differ from their 15-digit text (0.1+0.2, 1/3, 2/3, 1-1E-16), negative numbers, negative zero, the largest and smallest normal and subnormal doubles; each row's text equals Excel's.

## Out of scope
TEXT and number formats other than this conversion, cell display, locales other than en-US (cfml-m2.6).

title: Record instrumented evaluator calls independently of result publication and feed them to the verdict
description:
## Outcome
calc_verdict::judge counts a cell as calculated only against an evaluation record that an instrument on the evaluator produced, not against anything the result producer wrote. A result published without a recorded evaluation of its cell at its tick is unproven.

## Context
Follow-up of infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19, round-1 judge; plan 10.1: an engine status flag cannot establish that evaluation occurred, so provenance is reconciled against instrumented calls). infra-m1.1 takes the evaluation record as its own judge input, separate from the result set and in its own format, so the producer of results cannot write its own proof. Producing that record is this bead's work. The record is written by the instrument, not by the publication path that writes results. cfml-m1.3 (plans and frames) is where the hook belongs, and the same hook serves formula auditing (chost-m6.3). title: SQRTPI and other f64::powf sites take the platform pow: off Windows they can differ from Excel by one ULP
description:
## Outcome
calc-func's power-based kernels give Excel's bits on Linux and wasm as they do on Windows.

## Found by
The V3 sweep (dc-ns0) at b46c59a: `sqrtpi_kernel_matches_excel_num_on_internal_n_pi_overflow` failed in WSL. SQRTPI takes `f64::powf(0.5)`, which calls the platform runtime's `pow`. Excel's `(n*pi)^0.5` matches the MSVC runtime's `pow` (30/30 live samples, oxf-quxx), which is not correctly rounded; glibc's `pow` is, and at n = 0x7fd45f306dc9c882 gives 0x5fefffffffffffff where Excel gives 0x5ff0000000000000.

## Measured
On Windows, over 4,000,008 sampled products, MSVC `pow(p, 0.5)` differs from correctly rounded `sqrt(p)` at 2,030 (0.05%). Linux SQRTPI equals `sqrt` there, so it can differ from Windows at those inputs; whether Excel agrees with MSVC at every one of them is measured only at the 30 live samples. `excel_pow_chain` (x87) is not a substitute: it differs from MSVC `pow(p, 0.5)` at 3,772,247 of the same products.

## Do
- Port a form of the MSVC runtime's `pow` that reproduces its bits off Windows (or measure what Excel computes and port that), and use it at SQRTPI and the other `f64::powf` sites in calc-func that are meant to match Excel.
- Then make `sqrtpi_kernel_matches_excel_bits_at_the_last_finite_input` (now MSVC-only) run on every target.
close_reason: SQRTPI and all 30 f64::powf sites in calc-func now use a portable port of the Microsoft runtime's FMA3 pow, which is Arm's optimized-routines pow in its 256-entry configuration (tables confirmed entry for entry against ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100; MIT licence notice in crt_pow.rs): 0 differences against the real runtime in 8,000,000 random cases. The SQRTPI pin that was Windows-only passes on Linux (WSL, 434 calc-func lib tests). Evidence: cargo xtask check --wasm passed; Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272. Commit adf6780. Still open: the runtime's non-FMA3 pow (older CPUs) is not measured; other platform libm calls are the new libm bead.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: Function exactness lane, 2026-10-25 (adf6780): the Windows runtime's pow on every target. ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100.9711's FMA3 pow is Arm optimized-routines pow (fused multiply-add path, 256-entry exp, order-5 wide polynomial, narrow shift); its two tables equal Arm's entry for entry. excel_numeric/crt_pow.rs ports it (Arm 0b5e3775, MIT OR Apache-2.0) and all 30 f64::powf sites in calc-func call it. Against the runtime's own pow: 0 differences in 8,000,000 random cases over 8 regions (incl. square roots and SQRTPI's (n*pi)^0.5). Windows results unchanged (catalogue oracle cell for cell, Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272). sqrtpi_kernel_matches_excel_bits_at_the_last_finite_input runs everywhere; Linux (WSL) calc-func 434 of 434 lib tests pass. Still open: (1) the runtime's SSE2 pow on CPUs without FMA3, not measured; (2) the other platform-libm call sites (grep counts in src: ln 83, exp 18, sin 19, cos 13, sinh 10, cosh 9, log10 3, tan 2, atan2 2, tanh 1): the runtime's log/exp are AMD's table-driven routines, not Arm's. Measured against the correctly rounded value over 1,000,000 random arguments: Windows runtime ln 161, exp 4,936, sin 14,916, cos 17,755 differ; Rust's libm crate (the wasm32 libm; measured natively) ln 19,562, exp 77,741, sin 19,323, cos 16,033. BESSELY's order 0/1 lane (f64::ln; wasm ln(3) is one ULP below the runtime) is the one calc-func test this keeps native-only.

title: Platform libm calls in calc-func give target-dependent bits: match the Windows runtime everywhere
description:
## Outcome
calc-func gives the same bits on Windows, Linux and in the browser where it calls the platform's maths library (ln, exp, sin, cos, sinh, cosh and others outside the x87 route), matching what Excel on Windows computes.

## Found by
dc-8dg and dc-sbo (98046b0, adf6780): the x87 route and pow are now portable, but direct platform libm calls still differ by target. Windows' versions are AMD's hand-written routines in ucrtbase, not Arm's, so the pow approach does not carry over directly. Example: in the browser ln(3) is 1 ulp low, which puts BESSELY(3,0) 2 ulp off, so BESSELY stays native-only. Measurements are in dc-sbo's notes.

## Do
- List every platform libm call in calc-func and which Excel functions reach it.
- For each, either route it through the x87 chain Excel actually uses (if Excel's bits come from there), or port the Windows runtime's routine (reading its tables from ucrtbase.dll as dc-sbo did for pow), measured against the runtime over a large random sample.
- Turn BESSELY's test back to the browser pair.

## Acceptance
Per routine: differences against the Windows runtime over at least 1,000,000 random arguments; cargo xtask check --wasm passes with fewer native-only tests; Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272.
close_reason: calc-func no longer depends on the platform maths library: ln, exp, log10, sin, cos, sinh, cosh, atan2 and hypot (0f411cb, db30f10), with pow from adf6780, are ports of the Windows runtime's own routines and run on every target. Evidence: 0 differences against ucrtbase in 52,000,000 random arguments (at least 1,000,000 per region); BESSELY and the cos/sinh/cosh tests run in Chrome and Firefox again; Windows results unchanged; Ofgem 209,272/209,272; cargo xtask check --wasm passes, calc-func 490 tests in both browsers and 16 native-only. Still open: the runtime's non-FMA3 code path (only matters for matching Excel on CPUs without FMA3) is not ported.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: 2026-10-25 (exactness lane, DnaCalc-ceng): done in 0f411cb and db30f10. Every f64 libm call in calc-func product code (ln 88, exp 15, log10 2, sin 19, cos 12, sinh 6, cosh 6, atan2 2, hypot 1; powf since adf6780) now calls a port of the Windows runtime's FMA3 routine (ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100.9711: AOCL-LibM log/log10/exp/sin/cos/sinh/cosh/atan2 bodies, the runtime's own hypot), in excel_numeric/crt_libm.rs. Measured against the runtime with 1,000,000 random arguments per region: 0 differences in 52,000,000 (log/log10/exp 16M, sin/cos 14M, sinh/cosh 10M, atan2/hypot 12M). BESSELY's live-Excel test and the cos/sinh/cosh witness tests run in Chrome and Firefox again; cargo xtask check --wasm: calc-func 490 tests in the browsers, 16 native-only (each compares with x87 hardware or the MSVC runtime). Windows figures unchanged: oracle corpus 14,357 cells, pass 13,869, fail 488 (mismatched 299, refused 166, failed or missing 23); Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272. Still open: CPUs without FMA3 take the runtime's SSE2 bodies (not ported); the libm crate's erf/erfc/sqrt/log in normal_dist_common, special_dist_family and NORM.S.INV are deterministic across targets but not Excel's chain.

title: Excel's x87 arithmetic at native speed in the browser
description: On wasm and ARM, Excel's double-rounded + - * / run in the software x87 (about 64 ns per operation). A fast path: plain binary64 arithmetic plus an exact error term (TwoSum for add/sub, Dekker or FMA products for mul/div) that detects the rare cases where RN53(RN64(x)) differs from RN53(x), falling back to soft87 only there. Bit-identical to the hardware on hundreds of millions of random cases per operation, then Ofgem and the corpus in the browser.

title: Capture the array shape after recalculation and never record a spill as a scalar
description:
## Outcome
A capture records the array shape a formula has after Excel's full rebuild, and a formula that spills is refused or recorded as a spill, never as a scalar.

## Context
Follow-up of infra-m1.2 (2026-10-19, round-3 judge). platform/calc-oracle-excel/src/convert.rs decides dynamic_array or ordinary from the input package's ref only, and the worker compares saved and input formulas by cell key only (capture-worker.ps1, the saved-package checks). A formula that spills after the rebuild is therefore recorded as a scalar, against convert.rs's own doc and plan 10.1/10.2 (array shape is part of the comparison). infra-m1.3's round trip and the conformance beads compare these records. Infrastructure files only.

## Do
- Read Range.HasSpill and SpillingToRange through Get-ComProperty, or the saved package's ref and cm, for each formula cell.
- Refuse a spill until CaptureRecord carries its shape, or carry the shape in CaptureRecord version 2 and in calc-verdict's comparison.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-xb26 --platform windows --require-all
```
A stand-in or package case where a formula spills after the rebuild is refused or recorded with its shape, never as a scalar.

## Platforms
Windows (the worker), plus the platforms of calc-verdict if its record changes.

## Out of scope
Legacy CSE arrays as participants (infra-m7.4).
notes:
Started 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-ceng (br refuses the claim while infra-m1.2 is open; infra-m1.2's code is on master at 51471a2 and waits only on the owner's Excel steps). Changing the worker now, before the owner's first capture, avoids a recapture.
- Orchestrator ruling on the design: a formula cell that spills after Excel's full rebuild is recorded as a spill with its shape (the spill range's rows and columns, read from Range.HasSpill and Range.SpillingToRange through Get-ComProperty, and checked against the saved package's ref and cm), and its anchor value is never compared as a scalar. If CaptureRecord version 2 cannot carry the shape without changing calc-verdict's comparison, the cell becomes a typed per-cell spill failure that names the shape, and calc-verdict counts it as not comparable; the rest of the capture stays usable. Whole-capture refusal only if a spill's shape cannot be read.
- A cell whose input package says dynamic array but which does not spill after the rebuild is recorded as what Excel shows after the rebuild, with the input's claim kept.
- Cases: stand-in worker results (the existing worker_tests.rs and capture.rs test routes) for a spilling cell, a non-spilling dynamic-array cell, a spill whose shape cannot be read, and a package whose saved ref disagrees with SpillingToRange. No Excel run by agents; the excel route stays the owner's.
- What green does not show: Excel's own spill behaviour (the owner's capture under infra-m1.2/infra-m1.3).

Round 2 (2026-10-20): Acceptance and Platforms now include the owner's Excel route. The case dc_xb26__spill_shape declares windows and excel (platform/calc-oracle-excel/acceptance.json), and the bead closes only when both pass:

cargo xtask accept --id dc-xb26 --platform excel --require-all   (owner, on the Excel machine)

title: A file's unprefixed spelling of a prefixed function gives #NAME? on load, as in Excel
description:
## Outcome
A formula loaded from a file that spells a function Excel stores with a prefix (MAXIFS, MINIFS, IFNA and the other post-2007 functions) without that prefix gives Excel's result on load, the unknown-name #NAME?, while the same text typed by a user still computes; calc_fml tells file text from typed text and knows which functions take which prefix.

## Context
dc-besk's round-1 judge (2026-10-21): Excel 16.0 build 20430 shows #NAME? when it loads MAXIFS(Data!A1:A3,Data!B1:B3,"x") written without the prefix, and saves it back as _xludf.MAXIFS; dc-besk resolves the prefixed spellings, and its calc-host case shows the unprefixed file spelling computing 3. Telling the two apart needs two inputs from outside calc-fml's name lookup: catalogue metadata saying which file prefix each function takes (_xlfn., _xlfn._xlws.), which dc-552j's save half needs too, and a signal that a formula's text came from a file (calc-engine and calc-host compile loaded formulas; OneCalc compiles typed entry). Excel files never write such a formula; other tools may.

## Do
- Catalogue metadata: the file prefix each catalogued function takes, from Excel's own saved files.
- A load-origin input to calc_fml's compile (additive), passed by the routes that compile loaded formulas; a file-form call of a prefixed function without its prefix gives #NAME? as Excel's load does; typed entry is unchanged.
- Update dc-besk's calc-host case so its unprefixed rows expect Excel's result.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-besk --platform windows --require-all
```
A loaded package with MAXIFS and IFNA written without their prefix gives #NAME? for those cells; the prefixed spellings compute; typed =MAXIFS(...) computes.

## Out of scope
Writing prefixes on save (dc-552j).

title: Create the monorepo and isolated crate workspaces
description:
## Outcome
Create the monorepo and isolated crate workspaces. The behaviour is available through the Infrastructure production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements §§1, 10–13 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within Bootstrap checkpoint — independent lanes, CI and evidence safety. Own only Infrastructure files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: cargo xtask / calcctl; call the same exported library entrypoints as the applications.

## Do
Create one Cargo workspace with calc-value, calc-func, calc-fml, calc-doc-model, calc-doc, calc-engine, calc-host, dna-onecalc, dna-calc, xtask and platform adapter packages. Use one lockfile; every CI job and every agent checkout has its own target directory. Pre-create per-library tests and acceptance-manifest directories so four agents do not edit a shared registry. Commit the plan bundle (this plan, BEAD_GRAPH.md, BEAD_DETAILS.md, the JSONL exports, coverage.json and validate_plan.py) under docs/plan/ so every agent reads the text that bead Context sections cite, and commit the .beads/ tracker. Write AGENTS.md as the agent operating contract: claim a bead with br ready or bv --robot-next and br update <id> --status in_progress; run its acceptance and keep the receipt; one commit per bead on master with the bead ID in the message; br close with the evidence; file a follow-up bead instead of widening scope; all work on master as pull, work on one bead, commit, push, with no branches and no worktrees, ever; an agent working concurrently with another uses its own full clone of the repository on master (which gives it its own target directory), pulls before starting, and resolves a rejected push by pulling master and re-running its acceptance before pushing again; never two cargo invocations in one target directory at the same time; and the honesty rules from the brief (provenance before value, count every fallback, no faked behaviour, no seams without traffic, measure rather than assert).
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1
cargo check --workspace
cargo check --workspace --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --exclude calc-platform-desktop --exclude calc-oracle-excel --exclude xtask
```
- `infra_m0_1__workspace_builds`: Every portable package builds on the native targets and wasm32-unknown-unknown; prohibited OS imports fail the architecture test.
- `infra_m0_1__independent_lanes`: Four separate clones on master build Func, Fml, Doc and Engine modules concurrently, each in its own target directory, with no shared file writes.
- `infra_m0_1__agent_contract`: AGENTS.md names the claim, acceptance, commit and close commands, the master-only pull/work/commit/push rule with no branches or worktrees, and the one-cargo-per-target-directory rule, and docs/plan/ contains the plan text and bead exports that the bead descriptions cite.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution. Artifacts produced here are consumed by wasm/browser CI; this bead does not imply running a native CLI inside wasm.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: infra-m0.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Owner decisions taken at claim (2026-10-14), case text unchanged:
1. infra_m0_1__independent_lanes is a test in the xtask acceptance target. It clones the checkout it runs in (the local repository path, not GitHub) four times under the OS temp directory (%TEMP%\dnacalc-lanes\<n>), runs cargo check -p <crate> in all four concurrently, one each for Func (calc-func), Fml (calc-fml), Doc (calc-doc) and Engine (calc-engine), asserts four zero exits and no file writes outside each clone's target/, writes the four build logs into the receipt, and deletes the clones. A clone sees only committed work, so this case runs as its own sequential step after the build commit exists locally and before the push; workspace_builds and agent_contract are proven before the commit.
2. For infra_m0_1__workspace_builds, infra-m0.1 proves the builds; infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency proves the clause "prohibited OS imports fail the architecture test". infra-m0.1 may close before that clause is proven.

Receipt before infra-m0.3 exists: the retained command transcript under target/accept/infra-m0.1/, with command list and exit codes quoted in the close reason.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-14):
- Layout per plan section 1.3: crates/{calc-value,calc-func,calc-fml,calc-doc-model,calc-doc,calc-engine,calc-host}, apps/{dna-onecalc,dna-calc}, platform/{calc-platform-desktop,calc-oracle-excel}, tools/xtask. One root Cargo.toml and one committed Cargo.lock. No inter-crate dependency edges unless this bead's Do needs one; each later bead adds the edges it uses.
- infra_m0_1__workspace_builds must observe its result, not trust an exit code alone: it compares the workspace member set from cargo metadata with the expected package list (a removed member fails it), checks that every package outside the native-only set {calc-platform-desktop, calc-oracle-excel, xtask} was actually compiled for wasm32-unknown-unknown (for example from cargo's JSON compiler-artifact messages), and fails if the wasm check's exclude list drifts from the packages declared native-only. The native-only adapter packages refuse to compile for wasm32 (a compile_error! under cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")), so dropping one of their --exclude flags makes the wasm check fail.
- Cargo invoked from inside an acceptance test uses its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR (one cargo per target directory; the outer cargo test owns target/). Clone builds in independent_lanes run with --locked --offline so neither Cargo.lock nor CARGO_HOME is written.
- Acceptance case names are registered in a machine-readable manifest local to the xtask package; infra-m0.3's runner discovers per-package manifests, so every package gets its own (empty) manifest and tests directory now.

No package has a library API. Build commit 2d70eda, pushed.
Evidence: Windows (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, rustc/cargo 1.94.1), receipt target/accept/infra-m0.1/exit-codes.txt, all exit 0: cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1; cargo check --workspace; cargo check --workspace --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --exclude calc-platform-desktop --exclude calc-oracle-excel --exclude xtask; infra_m0_1__workspace_builds 1 passed (12 native and 9 wasm32 compiler artifacts compiled in the run, fresh=false); infra_m0_1__agent_contract 1 passed (AGENTS.md phrases, the 7 bundle files, 653 plan-section citations resolved); after the build commit, infra_m0_1__independent_lanes 1 passed (target/accept/infra-m0.1/L01-*, lanes.json): four clones of 2d70eda on master, each cargo's target directory read back as <clone>/target with CARGO_TARGET_DIR and CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR removed, four exit 0, four cargo processes alive together (each lane log shows waits on cargo's package-cache lock), no change outside each clone's target/, each target/ holding only its own package's build state, cargo home 33376 entries with no added, removed or changed path, source checkout HEAD and status unchanged; not measured: the OS temp directory outside the clones and the rustup home. description:
## Outcome

## Context
Implements §§1, 10–13 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within Bootstrap checkpoint — independent lanes, CI and evidence safety.
