Add required native test jobs, actual wasm-bindgen/browser test execution in Chromium and Firefox, desktop packaging smoke jobs and source/license checks. Pin toolchains and action revisions; archive logs and artifacts. Do not treat a wasm cargo check as executed tests.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p xtask --test acceptance infra_m0_2 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask ci-audit --require-executed-targets windows,linux,wasm
```
- `infra_m0_2__browser_failure_is_red`: A deliberately failing browser fixture makes CI fail rather than report a compile-only success.
- `infra_m0_2__platform_matrix`: Every portable crate and both app cores appear in a machine-readable executed-target manifest.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution. Artifacts produced here are consumed by wasm/browser CI; this bead does not imply running a native CLI inside wasm.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: infra-m0.2. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Handover from infra-m0.1 (2026-10-14):
1. No toolchain is pinned: there is no rust-toolchain.toml and no rust-version. Windows ran rustc and cargo 1.94.1, the WSL Ubuntu clone 1.93.1. tools/xtask/tests/acceptance.rs needs Rust 1.88 or later (edition 2024, let-chains). The orchestrator installed the wasm32-unknown-unknown target in WSL Ubuntu on 2026-10-14 for infra-m0.1's Linux run.
2. infra_m0_1__independent_lanes requires the checkout to be on master (git symbolic-ref HEAD) with an empty git status, because it clones HEAD. A CI checkout on a detached HEAD fails it, so CI checks out master by name for that case.
3. `cargo xtask ci-audit --require-executed-targets windows,linux,wasm` (this bead's Acceptance) is not built by infra-m0.3; the runner there implements only `accept`. This bead owns the ci-audit subcommand.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-14):
- GitHub state: DnaCalc/DnaCalc is private, default branch master; Actions are enabled with all actions allowed; the gh token on this PC has repo and workflow scopes. The WSL clone has no gh. CI's ubuntu job is therefore the Linux route for this bead's own Linux evidence (work prompt: once infra-m0.2 exists, Linux and browser evidence may come from CI, read with `gh run view` and downloaded into target/accept/<bead>/).
- One source of truth: each CI job checks out master by name (not a detached HEAD), takes the toolchain from a committed rust-toolchain.toml, and runs one repository command, `cargo xtask ci <job>`. It uploads target/ci and target/accept as artifacts with `if: always()`. The workflow file holds no test logic of its own. Actions are pinned by full commit SHA with the version tag in a comment. wasm-bindgen-cli is pinned at =0.2.117 (the runner's banner rule depends on it), and the job records chromedriver, geckodriver, Chrome and Firefox versions.
- rust-toolchain.toml pins the Windows toolchain version 1.94.1 with the wasm32-unknown-unknown target and the rustfmt and clippy components. rustup then installs that version in the WSL clone on first use; the commit message names this.
- `cargo xtask ci windows|linux` runs the architecture checks and every package's native tests (`cargo test --workspace --locked`). It writes target/ci/<job>/executed-targets.json listing every workspace package with built, test-harness-ran and tests-run/passed counts parsed from libtest lines. A package with zero tests is listed with 0 (visible, never counted as a pass). It also runs `cargo xtask accept --id <id> --platform <job> --require-all` for each ID in DNACALC_CI_ACCEPT, a workflow_dispatch input, and collects those receipts.
- `cargo xtask ci wasm` runs every portable package's wasm test targets under wasm-bindgen-test-runner in Chrome and Firefox through the runner's browser-forcing and banner rule (dc-e8ql). It records per package and per browser in the same manifest shape. With DNACALC_CI_INJECT_BROWSER_FAILURE=1 (a workflow_dispatch input) it adds a deliberately failing browser fixture, and the job must then fail at that step.
- Desktop packaging smoke: no desktop application exists yet. The job builds the native-only packages in release mode on Windows and Linux, uploads them, and records that no desktop package exists; a real packaging smoke starts when the application beads provide one (dnacalc-m8.1). Source and license checks: `cargo xtask ci licenses` checks that every dependency comes from crates.io (no git or out-of-workspace path source) and that its license expression is in a reviewed allow-list; it reports, without failing, that the workspace's own license is not yet chosen (an owner decision).
- `cargo xtask ci-audit --require-executed-targets windows,linux,wasm` merges executed-target manifests, either from a CI run (`--run <id>`, through `gh run download`) or from local directories (`--from <dir>`). It fails unless every portable package and both app cores appear as built with the test harness run on each required target, or if any recorded run failed.
- infra_m0_2__browser_failure_is_red: in a workspace copy, the case injects a failing browser fixture and runs `cargo xtask ci wasm`, the same command the CI job runs. It asserts a non-zero exit with the fixture named and the manifest marking it failed in each browser. It also parses .github/workflows/ci.yml and asserts that the wasm job runs exactly that command without continue-on-error. On a host without the runner or browsers it prints ACCEPT-NOT-RUN.
- infra_m0_2__platform_matrix: runs `cargo xtask ci` for the host target and wasm in a workspace copy and checks that every portable package and both app cores appear executed on those targets. The full three-target check is the bead's second Acceptance command, run against a real CI run.
- CI evidence the orchestrator collects after the push: a push-triggered run with every job green, with `cargo xtask ci-audit --require-executed-targets windows,linux,wasm --run <id>` exiting 0; a workflow_dispatch run with inject_browser_failure=true that ends failed at the wasm step; and a dispatch with accept_ids=infra-m0.2 whose ubuntu job (with browsers) runs the Linux accept, its receipt downloaded as accept-receipts/infra-m0.2/linux.json. The CI ubuntu image's preinstalled Chrome, Firefox and drivers may be used; record their versions.
Rulings after round 1 (2026-10-14, orchestrator):
- The second Acceptance command needs a CI run. The orchestrator runs it after the push as `cargo xtask ci-audit --require-executed-targets windows,linux,wasm --run <push run id>` and quotes it in the close. Add cargo-metadata dependency gates for OneCalc, skins and platform crates; deny tree-reference tokens and production-only dead seams using a reviewed call-site manifest plus integration coverage.

## Acceptance

cargo test -p xtask --test acceptance infra_m0_3 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all
```
- `infra_m0_3__zero_tests_fail`: A misspelled required test name fails the runner.
- `infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency`: Adding calc-engine to OneCalc or calc-host to CalcFml is rejected mechanically.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

notes:
Provisional plan ID: infra-m0.3. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Handover from infra-m0.1 (2026-10-14):
1. Owner decision 2 on infra-m0.1: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency also proves the infra_m0_1__workspace_builds clause "prohibited OS imports fail the architecture test" (plan section 1.3, last bullet: native COM, XLL and desktop filesystem implementations do not enter portable library or browser builds). 2. The native-only packages (calc-platform-desktop, calc-oracle-excel, xtask) carry compile_error! under cfg(target_arch = "wasm32"). No named case asserts that refusal yet: removing a compile_error! leaves every infra-m0.1 case green. Add the assertion to the architecture checks.
3. This bead adds the `cargo xtask` alias (.cargo/config.toml, which must not set build.target-dir) and updates AGENTS.md with the runner commands; the AGENTS.md Bootstrap note says so.
4. infra-m0.1 created the manifest format (AGENTS.md, Workspace section): per-package acceptance.json {"package", "beads": [{"id", "cases", "commands"}]}, cases in tests/acceptance.rs (test target `acceptance`). The runner extends the format (platforms, test target) and replaces the bootstrap form `cargo test -p <package> --test acceptance -- --exact <case> --nocapture`.
5. The default unit-test and doc-test harnesses of every library package print "running 0 tests"; the runner must never count them as executed cases.

7. Banned-word scan: docs/plan/ULTRACODE_WORK_PROMPT_OPUS_5_5.md states the rule and so contains both words; several imported tracker titles use the banned process noun (this bead's own title, infra-m3.20 to infra-m3.24 and others), and the case name infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate is a fixed identity.   (c) native-only packages refuse wasm32: each native-only package fails to compile for wasm32-unknown-unknown;
  (d) tree-reference tokens from a reviewed deny list seeded from plan sections 1.1, 1.3, 4.2 and 11.1 (tree reference, TreeRef, tree_ref, reference profile, ReferenceProfile, profile_id, ReferenceSystemProvider, host reference and their case variants) are absent from portable sources;

  (f) word scan: the two banned words of docs/plan/ULTRACODE_WORK_PROMPT_OPUS_5_5.md section 0 over docs/, AGENTS.md, README.md, tracker text (titles, descriptions, notes, close reasons) and commit messages. Fixed identifiers such as infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate are excluded by name. Occurrences that existed on 2026-10-14 (about 50 across 10 docs/plan files, 11 imported tracker records, no commit message) go into a committed baseline with per-file and per-record counts that every run reports; any occurrence beyond the baseline fails. The baseline is a counted fallback owned by a follow-up bead created now.
- Each check has a negative fixture showing it rejects: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency covers (a), (b) and (c) (adding calc-engine to dna-onecalc or calc-host to calc-fml, an OS import in a portable package, a native-only package without its wasm32 refusal). (d), (e) and (f) are proven by unit tests of the kind this package keeps, on fixtures under tools/xtask/tests/fixtures/, never by editing the real workspace.
- New dependencies only as the Do needs them, each named in the commit message (for example syn for (e)).

Rulings after round 1 (2026-10-14, orchestrator):
- Check (e) keeps the manifest half here; the coverage half (proving the named case reaches the caller, and refusing callers inside the defining library) is owned by dc-pz3u. seams.rs cites it and every receipt counts the seam entries whose reach is unproven.

- (d) scans non-test, non-comment Rust code of portable packages including build.rs; tests/, benches/, examples/, #[cfg(test)] code and comments are out of its scope by design and the check's text says so. include!, include_str! and include_bytes! are not followed: (b) and (d) fail when a portable package uses one, until a bead extends them to follow it.

title: Unify cache and live-oracle verdicts
description:
## Outcome
Unify cache and live-oracle verdicts. The behaviour is available through the Infrastructure production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context

Track formula denominator, calculated count, correct count, stale/not-modeled/missing/uncertified categories and type-aware comparisons. cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `infra_m1_1__cached_value_trap`: A file-cache-only result is counted as not calculated even when numerically equal to the expectation.

The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: infra-m1.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

From infra-m0.6 (2026-10-18): migration/evidence/oxfunc-smart-fuzzer.json gives each legacy capture folder a certifies_exact_target field. It is a known Excel build, which certifies only that build, or null for unknown, which certifies no Exact target. The verdict path must take this record as an input and refuse certification from an entry whose field does not name the selected target. Nothing consumes the field yet.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-19, DnaCalc clone, infra lane):
- Package. The verdict library is a new portable package, tools/calc-verdict (infrastructure-owned; plan 10.1 asks for "a portable verdict library"). It has its own acceptance.json and seams.json, and tests/acceptance.rs holds the two named cases, registered for windows, linux and wasm. The AGENTS.md workspace table and infra_m0_1__workspace_builds' expected member list gain it. Both are infrastructure files, so this bead edits them, and every closed bead's acceptance is re-run before the push. It depends on no CalcFml, CalcEngine, CalcHost, CalcDoc or application package. calc-value is allowed if it is needed for value types. An architecture.json closure rule records that.
- One verdict path. The library is the only place a verdict is computed. A file-cache replay and a live capture both feed it CaptureRecords, and its consumers (infra-m1.2's capture adapter, infra-m1.3's round trip, infra-m7.4, and later the product conformance command) call it rather than computing verdicts themselves. Production route: a `cargo xtask verdict` command that reads canonical CaptureRecord and result files (JSON, with numbers as binary64 bits in hex per plan 10.1) and writes a CellVerdict report. It calls the same library entry points the applications will.
- Provenance first. The library defines its own input vocabulary for a result's provenance: calculated, with its tick and context; file-cached; stale; not-modeled; and missing. It never accepts a status flag from the code under test as proof of calculation. CalcEngine's ValueProvenance (plan 2.2) maps onto it at the boundary when the engine exists (the ceng and chost beads). Only calculated results can be scored as matched. A file-cached value that equals the expectation is counted as not calculated, which is the cached_value_trap. Every category is counted: denominator, calculated, matched, mismatched, stale, not-modeled, missing, failed, not-run and uncertified.
- Observations. ExcelRawObservation (raw Value2 bits with the Excel build and settings), ExcelSavedCache (decimal <v> text, an observation and never a guaranteed binary64 oracle) and unknown-freshness caches stay distinct (plan 10.1). Strict-bit certainty is marked separately and comes only from a raw observation whose Excel build matches the selected target. Legacy evidence whose certifies_exact_target does not name the target (migration/evidence/oxfunc-smart-fuzzer.json, from infra-m0.6) is uncertified. Comparisons are type-aware: numbers by bits for strict certainty, text and booleans by equality, error identity, and array shape.
- Denominator integrity. The formula denominator comes from the independently enumerated formula inventory carried in the CaptureRecord, never from the set of results the evaluator returned. Hidden sheets, every cell of a shared-formula range (master and children), and error-valued formulas stay in it. A formula without a result is counted missing, never dropped.
- Port. DnaTreeCalc/src/dnacalc-conform/src/verdict.rs and OxFunc/smart-fuzzer/engine/src/{judge,classify}.rs are pinned for this bead (`cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` gives each disposition, and a reference input is read for behaviour only). The quarantine reading rule of infra-m0.5 applies. Port nothing from an input whose lookup exits 3 or 5; record any port in migration/ports/infra-m1.1.json.
- Cases. Both run in the browsers too. The fixtures are authored canonical CaptureRecord and result JSON that a test reads with include_bytes!. The assertions compare the report's counts and per-cell verdicts with literal values. Each case also shows its rule failing on a variant: the same value with calculated provenance is counted as matched, and a result set that leaves out a hidden-sheet formula still reports it missing.
- Class: refuters and judge at xhigh effort, and a mutation probe after the build commit, because this library carries the central provenance rule.
Rulings after rounds 1 and 2 (2026-10-19):
- The evaluation record is a separate judge input in its own format, which the result producer does not write. Producing it from instrumented evaluator calls is dc-qguw, which blocks infra-m1.3.
- Round 2 closed with no blocking finding. The orchestrator added the four legacy items that were not carried to migration/ports/infra-m1.1.json's not_ported list: OpenFailed, SheetUnmatched, EngineReadFailed and Degraded provenance.
- Follow-ups:
  - dc-sb69: certification and consistency rules (one build comparison, unattested parts and calculation settings, a replay claiming a saved cache, case-insensitive sheet names, expectations on the registered verdict commands, seams reach).
  - dc-u9ss: one shared JSON reader.
  - Notes on infra-m1.2 (CaptureRecord version 2 carries the revision, context fingerprint and shared ranges, and judge checks results.run against them), dc-qguw (the evaluated value or its hash), infra-m7.4 (array anchors, participants, volatile exclusion) and cfml-m1.3 (the evaluation hook).

## Out of scope

notes:
Provisional plan ID: infra-m1.2. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Hand-off from infra-m0.4 (2026-10-14; a change from plan section 10.2, flagged for the owner's M0 review): plan section 10.2 says infra-m0.4 resolves the exact capture-runner files. infra-m0.4 instead recorded every file under the source-discovery paths OxFunc/smart-fuzzer/ and OxFunc/tools/xll-addin/ as reference (oracle-runner category), and marked 30 runner_candidate inputs that drive Excel: 11 smart-fuzzer/tools PowerShell runners (CellRefBatch.psm1, Run-*.ps1), 13 smart-fuzzer/tools/w111 probes, calc_graph_racer/src/bin/race_effect_rri_check.rs (quarantine_derived) and 5 tools/xll-addin run-*.ps1 scripts. This bead selects the exact runner files among them when it ports (list them with `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup`), and records the selection by re-pinning through an Infrastructure disposition bead so the manifest names them for this bead.

From infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19): calc-verdict's CaptureRecord version 1 carries no authored revision or operations, no calculation-context fingerprint, no capture-tool revision, no output hashes and no capture failures, and calc-verdict has no encoder for CaptureRecord or ResultSet yet. Plan 10.2's capture manifest needs all of these, so the live capture adapter introduces CaptureRecord version 2 in calc-verdict (an infrastructure package), and the verdict keeps reading version 1. NumericTargetId's excel_build is free text, so certification compares build numbers by the rule calc-verdict documents.

From infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19, round-2 judge): stale detection trusts the run identity the result set declares (tools/calc-verdict/src/verdict.rs:529-546), because neither the evaluation record nor CaptureRecord version 1 carries an independent revision or context. A result set declaring revision R while the workbook is at R+1 is counted calculated. CaptureRecord version 2, which this bead introduces, carries the authored revision and the context fingerprint, and judge checks results.run against them: a case where a result set at R is judged against a capture at R+1 reports stale. Version 1 also has no shared-formula range (capture.rs:245-249), so a record listing C1 and C2 of C1:C3 passes with a denominator one short. Version 2 carries the shared range's ref, and judge refuses a record whose listed cells do not cover it.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-19, DnaCalc clone, infra lane):
- Files and route:

  - CaptureRecord version 2 (encoder and decoder) goes in tools/calc-verdict, an infrastructure package. The verdict keeps reading version 1.
  - There is one capture implementation. The worker is either a PowerShell COM script shipped inside calc-oracle-excel or Rust COM through the `windows` crate (a new dependency, license reviewed in tools/xtask/licenses.json); the implementer chooses and records the reason. Legacy runners stay readers or converters only.
- Excel is never started by an agent: `--platform excel` is the owner's run. The prepared state follows work prompt section 5.1:
  - the adapter and the replay code compile;
  - the replay case runs against the capture path and returns a typed MissingCapture, which the runner reports as not_run (so --require-all stays red for this bead);
  - no capture-shaped fixture is authored;
  - the fixture workbooks are authored;
  - the bead stays in_progress with a handover that names the owner's exact command and clone.
- Isolation:
  - one worker process per capture;
  - a fresh Excel instance from the worker, with DisplayAlerts off, AutomationSecurity set to force-disable, EnableEvents off, AskToUpdateLinks off and UpdateLinks 0 on open, and no add-ins loaded;
  - the calculation policy is set explicitly, recalculation is forced (a full rebuild), and the workbook is saved and then reopened.
  - The adapter records the PID of the Excel instance its worker started, from Application.Hwnd. On timeout it kills that worker and that Excel PID, and never any other Excel process, so the owner's own Excel survives.
- What is captured: raw Value2 number bits; the formula text, type and error codes; and the Excel build, version, compatibility, CPU, OS, locale (International), date system (Date1904) and calculation settings (Calculation, Iteration, MaxIterations, MaxChange, PrecisionAsDisplayed).
- CaptureRecord version 2 adds what infra-m1.1 left out:
  - the authored revision and operations;
  - the calculation-context fingerprint;
  - the capture-tool revision;
  - input and output package hashes;
  - capture failures;
  - each shared-formula range's ref.
  judge checks results.run against the capture's revision and context, so a result set at R judged against a capture at R+1 is stale, and it refuses a record whose listed shared cells do not cover the range's ref.
- Case infra_m1_2__untrusted_workbook has two parts:
  - windows: the isolation mechanism, with a stand-in worker that hangs. On timeout, only that worker and its Excel PID stand-in are killed, and a sentinel process standing for another Excel stays alive;
  - excel (the owner's run): a fixture with an auto-run macro that would write a marker, and an external link. After capture, the marker is absent and the link was not refreshed.
- Case infra_m1_2__capture_replays: a capture artifact produced by the owner's excel run is committed in small form, and replays through calc-verdict to identical verdict records on Windows, Linux and wasm (Chrome and Firefox). Until that capture exists, the case reports ACCEPT-NOT-RUN with MissingCapture, never passed.
- Fixtures: authored as files. A macro-enabled fixture may need a vbaProject part; if no honest way to author one exists without Excel, the handover asks the owner to author that one fixture in Excel and names the file.
- Lineage: run `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` for each of the 30 runner_candidate inputs (infra-m0.4 hand-off). Port nothing from an input whose lookup exits 3 or 5; the smart-fuzzer runners CellRefBatch.psm1 and Run-W109BulkBatch.ps1 are recorded unresolved (tainted-commit). Record the selection, or that none qualifies and the worker is written fresh from Excel's documented object model, in migration/ports/infra-m1.2.json. A re-pin is needed only if a runner is ported.
- Class: refuters and judge at xhigh effort, and a mutation probe after the build commit (security and isolation).

Correction to the claim note's isolation list (round 3, 2026-10-19): the worker sets no AskToUpdateLinks and no other option of the owner's Excel profile. It opens the workbook with UpdateLinks 0, which never refreshes a link, and records AskToUpdateLinks and IgnoreRemoteRequests as read. It does not unload add-ins: it reads every add-in's state and refuses the capture, before the workbook opens, when one is open, installed or connected, when one's state cannot be read, or when XLL functions are registered. A capture therefore needs an Excel profile with no loaded add-ins. The settings it sets (Visible, DisplayAlerts, ScreenUpdating, EnableEvents, Interactive, AutomationSecurity, and the calculation settings) belong to its own Excel instance or to the workbook it saves in the capture's work directory.

Handover to the owner (2026-10-19). The prepared state is committed at 10f2a42, and the bead stays in_progress. Every step below runs in C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc on master, after a pull. These are the owner's steps: no agent starts Excel.

1. Decide the add-in policy. As this PC's Excel profile stands, the worker refuses the capture before the workbook opens. The profile has two XLL add-ins under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Excel\Options (OPEN and OPEN1) and three HKLM COM add-ins with LoadBehavior 3. The worker refuses any add-in that is installed, open or connected, and refuses registered XLL functions; it switches nothing off. Either:
   (a) Take the capture under a profile with no such add-ins: unload them in Excel (File > Options > Add-ins) for the capture, or use a separate Windows user. Or:
   (b) Ask for the check to be narrowed to add-ins that are actually loaded in the automation instance (IsOpen, Connect, registered functions). That is a code change, with its own review.
   Not measured: whether an Excel started through automation loads these add-ins at all.

2. Author platform/calc-oracle-excel/tests/fixtures/infra_m1_2/untrusted-macro.xlsm in Excel, following the numbered steps in the module documentation of platform/calc-oracle-excel/tests/acceptance.rs. It needs a VBA project with Workbook_Open, Auto_Open and the user-defined function MarkUdf; =MarkUdf() goes in Sheet1!C1, and A1 must still be 1 when the workbook is saved. Delete any macro-ran.txt that authoring wrote, then commit the .xlsm.

3. Capture the replay fixture:
   cargo xtask capture --fixture platform/calc-oracle-excel/tests/fixtures/infra_m1_2/replay.xlsx --case infra_m1_2__capture_replays --out tools/calc-verdict/tests/captures/infra_m1_2/replay.capture.json --verdict tools/calc-verdict/tests/captures/infra_m1_2/replay.verdict.json
   Exit codes:
   - 0: the record and its verdict were written, replacing the two dnacalc-capture-absent markers. Commit both files.
   - 1: the capture failed, including the worker's own refusals (a loaded add-in, a setting that did not read back); the message says which.
   - 3: timed out (the worker and its Excel were terminated).
   - 4: Excel is not available.
   - 5: the completed record was refused for an isolation failure; it is kept in the work directory under target/capture/.
   The record carries the Excel build, channel, CPU name, OS, culture, International settings and add-in file names, never a path.

4. Run the excel route:
   cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.2 --platform excel --require-all
   It captures untrusted-link.xlsx and untrusted-macro.xlsm and checks that no macro ran, that the user-defined function did not run and that the link was not refreshed. Commit accept-receipts/infra-m1.2/excel.json, whatever its result.

5. Then the orchestrator re-runs windows, linux and wasm accept, so infra_m1_2__capture_replays compares the committed capture on every platform, and closes the bead.

Not measured yet:
- Workbook.CompatibilityVersion on your build.
- Whether a Click-to-Run configuration is present. If either is missing, the record carries an environment failure and every comparison against it is uncertified.
- Excel's edition is not recorded.

Mutation probe after the build commit 10f2a42 (2026-10-19, workflow wf_ad95eced-bf1; result in target/accept/infra-m1.2/mutation-probe.json of the DnaCalc clone, not committed). Twelve core-code breaks, each followed by `cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.2 --platform windows --require-all` against the baseline (not_run: 1 passed, 1 not run, commands 3 run, 0 failed). All twelve turned the run failed:
- The named case infra_m1_2__untrusted_workbook caught two: a PID in the pre-run snapshot taken as owned (the sentinel was terminated), and an owned Excel left running on timeout (Win32_Process found the stand-in still running).
- The other ten were caught only by unit tests inside the registered commands:
  - a reported PID of another image taken as owned (the test harness terminated itself, so no failing test is named);
  - package refusals off;
  - the add-in refusal off;
  - AutomationSecurity 1;
  - a null max_change formatted as bits 0;
  - the stale-revision check off;
  - the shared-range cover check off;
  - a multi-cell array taken as a single-cell dynamic array;
  - cargo xtask capture writing a record with an isolation failure;
  - DNACALC_ACCEPT_PLATFORM not set.
- infra_m1_2__capture_replays stayed not_run (MissingCapture) throughout, so it caught nothing until the owner's capture exists.
- No Excel process ran at any check, and the tree was restored to 10f2a42.

Update 2026-10-19 (51471a2): handover step 1 (the add-in policy) is resolved without the owner. The worker now refuses only add-ins loaded in the capture's own Excel instance (IsOpen, a connected COM add-in, unreadable state, registered XLL functions); add-ins installed in the profile but not open are recorded and do not refuse. The owner's remaining steps are 2 to 4: author untrusted-macro.xlsm, capture replay.xlsx, and run the excel route.

title: Ship the engine-free OneCalc application controller
description:
## Outcome
Ship the engine-free OneCalc application controller. The behaviour is available through the DNA OneCalc production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements §§2, 4, 8 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within First functional milestone — real Excel open/recalc/edit/save/reopen. Own only DNA OneCalc files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: the OneCalc application controller with its in-memory reference provider, never CalcEngine.

## Do
Build OneCalc controller plus a minimal desktop/browser surface with formula text, typed inputs, result, diagnostics and trace. Implement a small typed workbook/sheet/name provider for references; keep CalcEngine and CalcHost absent even from transitive dependencies.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
OxFml/crates/oxfml_core/src/eval/mod.rs: compiled expressions and evaluation; OxFml/crates/oxfml_core/src/binding/profile.rs: ReferenceNormalFormKey, ReferenceFingerprintPolicy. Discard ReferencePolicy, host-reference syntax and the tree profile.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p dna-onecalc --test acceptance onecalc_m1_1 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id onecalc-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id onecalc-m1.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id onecalc-m1.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `onecalc_m1_1__reference_without_engine`: A formula reads two explicitly supplied cells and calculates correctly with only CalcFml/CalcFunc.
- `onecalc_m1_1__dependency_gate`: cargo metadata for the full OneCalc package graph contains neither calc-engine nor calc-host.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox. Run the same semantic fixtures on every target; platform adapters also have their native integration tests.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: onecalc-m1.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Started 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cdoc (br refuses the claim while cfml-m1.3 is open; cfml-m1.3's evaluator is on master at a73bf20). This is the first application a person can use.
- Port: OxFml eval/mod.rs is exit 6 (calls_quarantined OxFunc oxfunc_core) and is already ported as calc_fml's evaluator; this bead consumes calc_fml::compile/instantiate/evaluate and ports nothing. Written fresh; say so in migration/ports/onecalc-m1.1.json only if something is taken from a pinned file.
- The capability to show:
  - A headless OneCalc controller in apps/dna-onecalc: a session holds typed inputs (sheet, cell, value: number, text, logical, error, blank), named sheets, and one formula text. Recomputing compiles through calc_fml::compile (a PlanCache the session owns), evaluates through calc_fml::evaluate over a small typed fixture provider (the session's ReferenceCatalog and ReferenceReader; an input the session does not hold is explicitly missing, never fabricated), and returns the result value, the diagnostics (parse diagnostics with their spans, binding refusals, EvalFault and FunctionFault, each typed and located), and a trace (the areas the evaluation asked the provider for, in order, with what it returned). No CalcEngine and no CalcHost, even transitively.
  - A minimal browser surface over that controller, mountable into a DOM element: a formula text box, a small table of typed inputs, the result, the diagnostics and the trace, updating on input. UI stack per plan section 1 (Leptos, CSR), with an exact version pin compatible with the workspace's wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and every new crate's license reviewed in tools/xtask/licenses.json. If Leptos cannot be pinned against wasm-bindgen 0.2.117, build the surface on web-sys and state why; the controller is the same either way. The page entry, index.html and site packaging are dc-gh6q.11's; the desktop shell is dnacalc-m2.1's.
- Cases:
  - onecalc_m1_1__reference_without_engine: a formula reads two explicitly supplied cells (one on another sheet) and calculates correctly, through the controller, with the trace showing the two reads; a third run with one input removed shows the missing input as a typed diagnostic or value, not a fabricated one. In the browsers the same case mounts the surface in a test element, sets the inputs and the formula through dispatched input events, and reads the result and trace text from the DOM.
  - onecalc_m1_1__dependency_gate: cargo metadata for dna-onecalc's full package graph (all features, every target the architecture check uses) contains neither calc-engine nor calc-host; native platforms only.
- What green does not show: agreement with Excel (cfunc-m1.2's capture), the published page (dc-gh6q.11), the desktop package (dnacalc-m2.1).

Handover 2026-10-20: built e24e1e3, fix 2393f2f (long sheet names no longer overflow the label code). Evidence: windows and wasm (Chrome and Firefox) --require-all 2 of 2 and 1 of 1 at the 2393f2f tree; linux --require-all passed at 2393f2f in WSL (crates from the vendored copy; WSL has no network), with cargo test -p dna-onecalc and infra-m0.3 linux. The judge withheld close only for the defined-name gap, now dc-lgqh (after cfml-m3.1). An independent reviewer of the orchestrator's post-judge edits found the overflow and a wrong comment, both fixed in 2393f2f with the overflow names added to the unit test (restoring the old fold fails it); the dependency case was confirmed real by two mutation probes. br refuses the close only because cfml-m1.3 is open. Cite e24e1e3 and 2393f2f at close; name dc-lgqh under Still open.
